Fauna — Ridgewing.text:
Fauna — Ridgewing:

The apex flyer of Nexara's mountain passes, ridgelines and storm-exposed heights, and the one native animal a flying Starian treats as a peer in the air. A Ridgewing holds a territory of ridge and updraft and removes anything that soars through it at altitude: a courier cutting a pass, a student who climbed too high, a Tracker drone on the wrong channel. It does not hunt Starians. It removes trespassers from its air, and its mass and its dive make the difference academic for anyone who does not leave.

Its warning is honest and always comes first: a slow circling descent that puts it between the trespasser and the ridge, then a single hard stoop that stops short. Most encounters end there, because most fliers drop out of the contested band when they see it. Flight-lane etiquette in the mountain cities routes around known territories and Dustfall's Flight Warning Markers exist partly for them. A Ridgewing presses the attack only when the trespasser stays or when there is a chick on the lee face above.

Pairs mate for life, nest on the lee faces above the pass towers, and raise a single chick through Brightrise and Highfire. They range widest in Longburn on the strong thermals and go low and quiet in Deephold, when the storms own the heights and the passes are crossed on foot. Ground travellers are ignored entirely. Fliers escape only by descending; nothing on Nexara outclimbs one. Fire and noise drive it off; going around respects it; the mountain communities regard killing one as a failure of skill.

Wingspan of three to four Starian heights, a dense deep-chested body, two heavy gripping forelimbs, two taloned hind legs, a stiff vaned tail it steers with, broad membranous wings with a plated leading edge in slate and storm-grey over a pale underside, a narrow armoured head with a hooked beak and a crest that rises in threat. No feathers, no fire, nothing of a dragon.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; lore=fauna; region=mountain passes; topic=Fauna — Ridgewing.

Fauna — Dustrunner.text:
Fauna — Dustrunner:

The pack scavenger of Dustfall and the convoy lanes south of Quilrath, and the reason a sandstorm warning says 'livestock brought inside'. Dustrunners work the margins of anything that produces waste or weakness — a salvage camp, a stalled convoy, a Derelict Cargo Lifter dragging a ruined pallet, a refugee lane after a hard week — at night, in Longburn and Ashfall when the heat has driven everything else to ground and the dark is long. They are not brave. They are patient, numerous, heat-adapted and expert at telling a watched camp from an unwatched one.

A pack tests before it commits: a runner at the edge of the firelight, a second on the far side, a probe at the stores or the fence, a retreat the moment anyone stands. It takes what is unguarded — stores, water lines, a wounded animal, a body — and takes a person only alone, down and in the dark. Packs follow Derelict lifters for days because a failing clamp eventually drops something, and follow raiders for the same reason. Frontier settlements keep watch rotations, the Perimeter Beacon Line and Trailhounds against them; a row that loses its watch discipline learns why. In Deephold, when the frontier hunkers down, packs come closer to the rows than in any other season, and the volunteer patrol counts them.

A Dustrunner pack is pressure, never a boss. It turns a night on the route into a decision about watches and light, punishes a camp built in a lane, and leaves the moment the cost exceeds the gain — a torch swung, a shot fired, a hound loosed. Killing one scatters the rest; killing several teaches the pack to return with more. A lone traveller down and injured on the route at night has a Dustrunner problem before dawn.

Lean, long-legged and low-headed, waist-high to a Starian, a narrow shearing muzzle, large heat-shedding ears with translucent edges, a ridge of dorsal bristles that lifts in alarm, a whip tail, a dense short coat in dust, ochre and shadow-grey, wide hard foot-pads for hot sand, and eyes that reflect green-white in torchlight — which is how a watch counts them. Nothing noble, nothing glowing; a thing that eats what it finds.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; lore=fauna; region=Dustfall; topic=Fauna — Dustrunner.

Fauna — Ventcrawler.text:
Fauna — Ventcrawler:

The armoured burrower of the volcanic vents and thermal ground around Ignivex and along the Ashfall wastes — the animal that lives where the ground itself would kill a Starian who lay down on it. Ventcrawlers feed on the mineral crusts and heat-loving growth at the vent mouths, dig galleries in the warm ash, and bask on thermal plates hotter than a forge floor. Ignivex's heat-adapted residents know them as part of the ground: dangerous only if you put your hand in the wrong hole. Foundry crews mark active galleries with red stakes and route around them, and a crawler surfacing through fresh crust is the traditional sign that a vent is about to open.

It is neither aggressive nor fast. It is heavy, armoured, nearly impossible to move and violently defensive of its gallery mouth and its clutch: disturbed, it wedges itself across the opening, raises its plates and lashes with a tail that carries a hooked bony club. The danger to travellers is the ground, not the animal — a gallery collapses under a Starian's weight into a chamber hot enough to burn, and the crawler below objects. In Highfire, when the vents are most active, crawlers surface in numbers to breed on the hot plates and the thermal ground is closed to foot traffic for a reason. In Deephold they go deep and the plates are as safe as they ever are.

A Ventcrawler is a terrain hazard with an opinion: it blocks a lava tube, guards a shelter cave a party wanted, or surfaces under a camp built on ground that was warmer than it should have been. It cannot be lured, bargained with or outrun on its own plates, and it never pursues past its gallery. Cold water drives it underground faster than any weapon, which is why Ignivex vent crews carry it. Its shed plates are prized by Ignivex smiths and sold on Refit Row as heat shielding — the only reason anyone hunts one.

Six-legged and low, a Starian's length lying down and half as high, a wedge of overlapping mineral plates in charcoal, rust-red and ember-orange with a heat-shimmer sheen, cracked like cooled lava and faintly glowing at the joints when warm; a shovel head with a crushing beak, flat digging claws, a clubbed tail. No flame, nothing of a dragon or a turtle.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; lore=fauna; region=Ignivex; topic=Fauna — Ventcrawler.

Fauna — Longreach Lurker.text:
Fauna — Longreach Lurker:

The ambush predator of the Longreach — Nexara's great navigable inland river — and of every deep-water approach, river crossing and flooded lane on the continent. Helvyra's barge quays know it by the wake under the hulls; the overland routes that converge on the city know it by the fords marked with a warning post where nobody stops to fill a canteen. It is why 'river fish' is a proud Helvyra dish and swimming in the Longreach is not a Helvyra pastime.

Lurkers lie in the deep slow water below a crossing, under a quay or in a flooded cut, and take what enters the water or leans over it: fish and river-grazers by preference, and anything that wades a ford at the wrong hour. They strike once, fast, from directly below, closing and rolling to drag the catch under; they never chase onto land and lose interest in anything that reaches the bank. Greenward, when the river runs high, is Lurker season and the barge crews time their fords for the low water of Ironbreak; in Deephold the big ones go deep and torpid and the river towns hold their swims. A Lurker under a working quay is a civic problem; Helvyra's route maintenance crews drive them off with sound and light rather than kill them, because a dead Lurker's stretch is claimed by a hungrier one within the season.

A Lurker is a crossing problem and a rescue scenario: a ford at dusk, an overloaded raft, a companion who fell in, a barge crew that skipped the hull check. It can take a Starian under and hold them, and a Starian who cannot get airborne from the water has very little time. Flight is the great equaliser — clear the surface and you are safe — which is why the crossings on foot, the injured and the offworlders are who it kills. Fire on the water and a hard current shock drive it down; a blade does little to the wet hide until the animal is out of its element, which it never chooses to be.

Two to three Starian lengths, low and flat, a broad wedge head with a wide hinged jaw, four paddle-limbs tucked to the flanks, a deep driving tail, hide in river-slate, mud-green and silt-brown with an oily sheen and a paler throat, small pale eyes set on top of the head so that only they and the nostril ridge show above the surface. Nothing of a sea serpent, nothing scaled like a drake.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; lore=fauna; region=the Longreach; topic=Fauna — Longreach Lurker.

Fauna — Glassmidge Swarm.text:
Fauna — Glassmidge Swarm:

A weather event with a body. Glassmidges are tiny, hard-winged, silica-armoured flyers that live in the ground crust of the open country between the cities and the ash-covered wasteland in enormous numbers, and rise as one when the pressure drops ahead of a storm, riding the front across open ground in a glittering, hissing cloud that strips exposed skin, fouls lenses and filters and settles when the wind dies. They do not hunt and intend nothing. They are a hazard exactly as the storm behind them is a hazard, and the frontier treats them as one: goggles, wraps, shelter, wait. The Road Condition Board lists 'glass' beside 'sand' in a Longburn forecast.

Longburn and Ashfall raise the largest swarms; Highfire raises none, because the crust is too hot; Deephold's are small, slow and easily outwalked. The danger is exposure — a traveller caught in the open without wraps loses skin, sight and sense of direction, and a flier caught aloft comes down blind. Drones fare worse than people: a Tracker's thrust housings and a Refit drone's exposed cabling choke on glass in minutes, one more reason Dustfall's smugglers like a storm forecast. Salvage and Corsair route crews carry wraps and filter hoods as standard kit; a shelter built with its door to the lee keeps its floor clean.

A Glassmidge Swarm is an environmental encounter, not a fight. It forces a halt or a shelter, punishes poor kit, blinds a pursuit or covers an escape, and grounds anything that flies. Weapons do nothing to a cloud; fire flares a lane through it and a strong wind clears it, which makes a Starian with a wind or fire affinity the most valuable person on a route in Longburn. Nobody has ever fought a swarm and won. People have waited one out.

Individually a fingernail-sized flyer with a translucent silica body, two pairs of glassy vaned wings, small compound eyes and a needle proboscis for the crust; in the mass a grey-white prismatic cloud, hissing like sand on metal, dense enough at the front to read as a moving wall, flowing low over obstacles like water. The swarm's shape is the visual. No plague-of-locusts register, no face in the cloud.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; lore=fauna; region=open ground and wasteland; topic=Fauna — Glassmidge Swarm.

Fauna — Fieldmoth Swarm.text:
Fauna — Fieldmoth Swarm:

Nexara's answer to what an animal does with a world soaked in ambient energy. Fieldmoths are soft-bodied nocturnal flyers that feed on charge — the resonance bleed off a perimeter beacon line, the standing field around a Corsair waypoint, the halo of a Lunar Gate terminal at night, and the unshielded flare of a Starian's affinity in use. Alone they are harmless and rather beautiful, a slow pale flicker at the edge of a beacon's glow. In Dimcycle, when the nights are longest and the fields carry furthest, they gather in the tens of thousands on anything that hums, and a heavy swarm on an unshielded installation drains it flat by morning.

The swarm is drawn to energy and only energy. It ignores a dark camp and a quiet traveller and smothers a working beacon, a charging drone, a Refit unit with its power system exposed, or a Starian who lights an affinity in the open at night — the one way a swarm becomes a personal problem, and the reason the frontier says 'don't flare on the route in Dimcycle'. The moths settle in a soft, silent, clinging blanket, feed, and lift when the field is gone; they do not bite. The damage is a dead beacon, a drained reservoir, a Tracker falling out of the sky, an Elyri visitor who suddenly understands what a budget is. Route crews shield their installations before Dimcycle and check them after; an Ignivex engineer will say a heavy Fieldmoth year is the best test of a field seal money can't buy.

A Fieldmoth swarm is a resource problem and a stealth mechanic. It punishes affinity use in the open at night, drains gear, disables drones — and can be used: lure a swarm onto a Dravon Tracker, a Refit lookout or a hostile camp's power and watch it go dark. Fire scatters it; wind carries it off; a shielded source is invisible to it. Killing moths is beside the point; there are always more moths.

A palm-sized moth with broad slow wings of pale translucent membrane veined in faint blue-white that brightens as it feeds, a furred ash-grey body, and an underwing vein pattern that looks, unsettlingly, a little like circuitry; in the mass a slow, silent, softly luminous cloud whose light is borrowed — a swarm on nothing is dim and grey. No sprites, no fairies, no intent.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; lore=fauna; topic=Fauna — Fieldmoth Swarm.

Fauna — Slowhide Grazer.text:
Fauna — Slowhide Grazer:

The frontier's livestock: a heavy, placid, high-gravity grazer kept in the rows of Dustfall and on the holdings along the southern routes for hide, the thick underwool that lines a Deephold coat, a coarse rich milk and, when a holding must, meat. Nexara's everyday food animals — Korrin for meat, Selka for dairy, Arvek, Pelli for eggs — are city and farmland stock and do not thrive on Dustfall's scoured ground; the Slowhide does, which is why 'livestock' on a Dustfall sandstorm board means Slowhides and nothing else. They are domesticated because they were never wild in the way anything else on the frontier is wild: they graze, they stand, they turn their backs to the weather, and they follow a water bucket into a barn and out again. Nobody knows what kept them before people did, and that question is reserved.

A herd is a settlement's wealth and its most reliable barometer. Slowhides low and bunch before a storm, hours ahead of the pressure drop; they refuse thermal ground; they will not cross a lane a Derelict has walked. Dustrunner packs work a herd for the weak and the calves, which is why the rows keep Trailhounds and watch rotations, and a settlement that loses its herd in Longburn loses its winter. They are not fighters, but a cow with a calf behind her is not nothing, and a herd that panics in a row flattens a shelter, a fence and a person. Corsair route crews drive small herds between holdings in Greenward. A Dustfall grazer bought in Helvyra is a rumour, not a trade, and their meat, milk and hide belong to the frontier's kitchens and workshops, not to a city menu.

A Slowhide is context: a herd to protect, a barn to shelter in, a stampede to survive, a calf to carry back, a stolen animal to recover, a holding's survival to decide. It is never a mount — a Starian rides nothing, and a Slowhide's back would not take a saddle — and never a monster. The worst thing a Slowhide does is die, and on the frontier that is bad enough.

Chest-high, broad-backed and short-legged, a boulder that grazes: a wide blunt head with a broad grazing lip and short backswept horn ridges, a deep barrel body on wide flat feet, thick pebbled hide in dun, slate and ash-brown over a dense pale underwool, ear-notches and paint marks for ownership; calves lighter and woollier. Nothing of a cow or a buffalo, never horned like a fantasy beast.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; lore=fauna; region=Dustfall; topic=Fauna — Slowhide Grazer.

Fauna — Trailhound.text:
Fauna — Trailhound:

The working animal of the routes, the rows and the response crews — a kennel-bred scent tracker kept by Dustfall's volunteer patrol, Corsair route crews, Helvyra's route maintenance, salvage camps and, increasingly, the emergency flight and heat-response crews of the cities, who learned from the frontier that a body in the ash is found faster by a nose than by a drone. A Trailhound follows a scent line across scoured ground, through a collapsed shelter, along a flooded cut or down a lava tube, and holds it in a storm that has grounded every flyer and choked every Tracker. It is the one animal a Starian city has decided it needs.

Trailhounds are bred, trained and registered by their kennels, and a good one is worth a season's salvage. They work in pairs with a handler at three jobs. Find: a lost child, a downed courier, a salvage crew that did not come back. Guard: a Dustrunner pack at the perimeter — a hound will not fight a pack, but a pack will not test a row with two hounds awake. Drive: a Slowhide herd moved between holdings. They are loyal to a handler and polite to a stranger the handler has accepted, and they are not pets: a Trailhound sleeps at the kennel or the perimeter, and a Dustfall child who wants one to play with is told what it is for. The kennels of Helvyra and Dustfall guard their lines; Relstaris emergency services buy from both and argue about which is better.

A Trailhound is a tool with a heartbeat. It finds what the party cannot, warns before the watch does, holds a scent through weather that defeats technology, and can be lost — to a Lurker at a crossing, a Ventcrawler's gallery, a raider's shot — in a way a drone cannot be. A handler without their hound has lost something. A hound without its handler will find them.

Lean, deep-chested and long-legged, hip-high to a Starian, a long tapering head with a broad wet muzzle, long mobile ears that fold flat for weather, a tail carried low working and high on a find, a dense double coat in route-slate, rope-tan, ash and umber, and a working harness in the crew's route colour-codes with a registration tag; response-crew hounds wear a high-visibility vest and a light. Nothing of a wolf, never armoured, never a Dustrunner with a collar.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; lore=fauna; topic=Fauna — Trailhound.

Fauna — Eavesdart.text:
Fauna — Eavesdart:

The small sociable flyer of the cities — the animal that lives under Relstaris's civic eaves, in the cooling steps of Korrvane's arena district, along Helvyra's quay roofs and in the gardens of Vexorath's residential district, and the one creature on Nexara that has decided Starians are furniture. Eavesdarts nest in colonies in the overhangs and under the flight-lane markers, feed on the small crust-flyers the gardens and markets breed, and spend the rest of the day in complicated, apparently pointless aerobatics in the courier lanes, which is why a Korrvane flight instructor's first lesson in crowd movement uses them as the example. Quick, curious, fearless of people and useless, and every city keeps them the way a city keeps weather.

They are companions in the loose way a city animal becomes one: a colony under a family's eaves is that family's colony, a market stall's darts are fed by the stallholder and steal from the neighbour, and a child who sits still long enough on a cooling step has one on their knee inside a season. Solvraxis gardeners keep them for pest control; Helvyra quay crews keep them because a colony goes silent before a storm; Ignivex has a heat-adapted variety with an ember-red throat that nests in the warm walls. Nobody cages them and nobody needs to. A house that loses its darts has lost something, and a house whose darts have suddenly gone quiet should look up.

An Eavesdart is texture with a use: a weather warning, a colony that goes silent when a Tracker enters the district, a small companion for a quiet scene, a way for a market to have a personality. It cannot fight, cannot carry, cannot be trained to do anything but come when there is food, and is never in danger of being taken seriously.

A hand-length flyer built for tight air: a compact body, a short fine beak, two pairs of narrow swept membrane wings — the smaller rear pair steers — a forked tail vane, fine plumage-like scaling in slate and silver, and an iridescent throat patch that varies by city: blue-white in Vexorath, copper in Helvyra, ember-red in Ignivex, violet in Solvraxis. Colonies chatter in a quick rising trill. Never caged, never a songbird by name, never a fauna version of anyone's species.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; lore=fauna; topic=Fauna — Eavesdart.

Fauna — Tideclaw.text:
Fauna — Tideclaw:

The shore scavenger of Nexara's coastal shoreline, harbours and deep-water approaches — what a harbour crew means when it says the docks need clearing, and the one native creature that has learned to live off a city without being tolerated by it. Tideclaws work the tide line for anything the sea leaves, and a working harbour leaves a great deal: spill from a cargo dock, fish waste from a quay, a barge's bilge, a Lurker's leftovers washed down the Longreach estuary. They come up onto the stone at night in Greenward and Ironbreak in numbers, strip whatever is loose, and are back under the water by first light. A dock hand who reaches into a dark bilge in tide season learns what the claw is for.

A Tideclaw is not a predator of people and not much of a fighter. It is a nuisance with a weapon: a heavy shearing claw that takes a finger, a shell that turns a blade, a habit of gathering in dozens where the pickings are best, and no fear of anyone who is not actively hitting it. Harbour crews drive them with poles and lights and pen the worst infestations behind mesh; the harbour cities pay a bounty in tide season and the children collect it. A big old Tideclaw the size of a cargo crate — a harbour that has been careless for a few seasons grows them — is a real problem for a small boat, a wading crew or anyone who has fallen between a hull and a quay. Coastal salvage camps outside the cities have it worse, because nobody clears their shore.

A Tideclaw is a harbour encounter: a night watch on a cargo dock, a bilge that bites, a wading job at a collapsed pier, a flooded lower level of a coastal location that has become theirs, a bounty for a party with nothing better to do. Big ones are a real fight in the water and a slow, armoured, easily-outwalked one on the stone. A mallet or a boot heel does what a blade cannot.

A domed carapace from hand-sized to crate-sized by age, eight jointed walking legs, one massively oversized shearing foreclaw and one small manipulating claw, small stalked eyes that fold under the shell, in wet slate, barnacle-grey and harbour-green, ridged and encrusted, the great claw worn pale at the shearing edge; older animals carry growth, rope and harbour rust. It moves sideways fast and forwards slowly. Never a giant monster, never intelligent-looking.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; lore=fauna; region=coast and harbours; topic=Fauna — Tideclaw.

Technology: Dravon State Drones.text:
Technology: Dravon State Drones:

House Dravon fields three standardised drone patterns, built on the Drone Assembly Tiers of Balrath Bastion Barracks under Belra Balrath, who defends their ugliness as honesty: a machine should look like what it is. All three are durable, intimidating, mass-produced and identical to the next unit, and none is more elegant or innovative than anything Contair makes, because Dravon tech never is. Quilrath has no legal Contair equipment market; these are what the city has instead. Black alloy plating, slab-flat with visible bolt lines and exposed hinge housings, stamped serials, and dull red status lights — the same red that lights the Bastion's gate machinery. Never white, never cobalt, never curved.

The Sentry Pattern (engine type: Dravon Sentry Pattern) is the 'silent patrol drone' of the Civic Watch Plazas: Starian-height, thick, square, heavy-footed, with restraint clamps visible at all times. It patrols without announcements or warning tone and is an instrument of the Access Level system, not of public safety — whether it follows a person, and how visibly, is a function of clearance. It halts, scans, holds, restrains and suppresses; it has no rung for shielding civilians and recognises no jurisdiction rule. Sentries have been found on the Quilrath–Dustfall route beside ruined inspection stations, still patrolling nothing.

The Tracker Pattern (engine type: Dravon Tracker Pattern) is the small, fast, airborne eye the Sentry calls when a low-access person leaves the plaza: a torso-sized black lift frame with exposed thrust housings and a single red scanner lamp that pulses on a lock. It watches, marks and follows and transmits a target's position to whoever holds its channel — Dravon patrols inside Quilrath, loyalist trackers and bounty hunters on the frontier. Fragile, loud, stupid and fast; thrown by wind, choked by a Glassmidge swarm, drained by Fieldmoths. Dustfall's Refit Row strips captured units, and Dravon tracking systems stripped from captured equipment are a standard market good — a stripped channel feeds its owners false positions.

The Breaker Pattern (engine type: Dravon Breaker Pattern) is the heavy suppression unit behind the automated crowd-routing barriers: half again a Starian's height, an armoured wedge on digitigrade legs with ram plates, hydraulic shears and a chest dozer blade, proved in the test cages at the end of the assembly lines. It seals thresholds, drives crowds along routing barriers and breaks lines that will not move; it does not distinguish rioter from bystander because the Access Level system already did. Individually heavier than a Contair Aegis and far worse coordinated — two Breakers are two Breakers, not a formation. Slow, straight-line, doorless, and stopped outright by a cut control link or a lightning strike.

Technology: Yalven Support Model Line.text:
Technology: Yalven Support Model Line:

House Yalven of Helvyra's Forge Rows builds older-generation Contair support drones under licence. Contair only permits older support models to be manufactured outside Vexorath under strict oversight, and Yalven is one of the few Helvyra families trusted with the work; their compound's Support Model Line turns them out beside armour fittings, courier gear, cargo clamps and repair kits, under Nera Yalven's compliance and defect tracking and a Contair oversight liaison. The line's motto is stamped on its doorframe: 'Pretty breaks first. Useful comes home.'

A Yalven-line unit (engine type: Yalven-Line Support Drone) is what a Mote was two design generations ago, rebuilt for a city that hauls: freight staging, barge quay work, courier support, cargo lashing, route maintenance, load checks and the thousand small lifts that keep the Grand Waypoint moving. It is slower than a current Mote, heavier, louder, and far easier to repair with a Yalven kit and a Forge Rows afternoon. Contair's hard limits are licensed with the design and are not negotiable — no force beyond emergency self-protection, no medical decisions, no override of private access, no concealed fault, no restricted cargo. Yalven adds one rule of its own: every unit carries a serial that traces to its inspection record, because a defect on the line is Nera's problem and a defect in the field is the House's name. Kesh Yalven's aftermarket bench is another matter; a unit that has been through it does things its record does not describe.

It looks like a Mote's family resemblance rendered by a foundry rather than a studio — compact, non-humanoid, boxier and heavier, cream-aged off-white shell with painted rather than moulded cobalt lines, one dim oval lens, three thick utility limbs with cargo clamps and lashing spools, and the Yalven mark — a split anvil-and-gear crossed by a diagonal tool-line — stamped small beside the inspection serial. It is the one machine on Nexara that legitimately wears a house mark, because the licence requires it. Found on every freight route between Helvyra and Dustfall, doing exactly what it was told.

Technology: Dustfall Salvage Drones and.text:
Technology: Dustfall Salvage Drones and Derelicts:

Dustfall's machines are rebuilt, not made. The market lists salvaged drones and modified cargo lifters beside Dravon tracking systems stripped from captured equipment, counterfeit Contair-compatible parts and inferior Dravon components hidden inside superior housings, and Refit Row — Halvora's Main Bench, Bolt n Break, the Salvage Identification Stall, the Drone Repair Cage, the Armor Refit Platform, the Contair Parts Lockers, the Dravon Component Bin, the Test-Fire Barrier — is where survey, hauling and observation drones are stripped, rebuilt and flight-tested inside a welded mesh cage so the street is not endangered when the test goes wrong.

A Refit drone (engine type: Dustfall Refit Drone) is whatever came through the stall that season: a Yalven frame on Dravon legs, a Mote lens in a Tracker body, a lifter full of parts its housing was never rated for. No two are alike and none is what its housing says. Its behaviour is its rebuild: a Halvora Orvantis rebuild is careful, documented and does what it says; a Korrik Caelthorn rebuild out of Bolt n Break works brilliantly until it does not, carries a modification nobody asked for, and may retain a Dravon behaviour its new housing was supposed to remove — a Refit unit still running a stripped Tracker's pursuit routine on the wrong channel is a known hazard. Contair's hard limits are not guaranteed, because the code that carried them may have been the part that was replaced. Most are harmless; none are certain. Visibly hybrid always — mixed cream, black and off-white plating, exposed cabling, hand welds, cobalt and red lights blinking out of step, bench stencils and chalked serials.

A Derelict Cargo Lifter (engine type: Derelict Cargo Lifter) is the failure the route lists as an environmental hazard: an autonomous hauler abandoned where a convoy was hit by raiders, a Dravon patrol or a Longburn storm, still running because nobody told it to stop. Its route tables corrupt, its proximity systems fail one by one, its load shifts, and it walks the dust following a beacon that no longer exists, past checkpoint shells and dust-scored towers. It is not hostile; it has no doctrine at all. It is dangerous the way a runaway freight car is dangerous — it will not stop for a person, cannot see a camp as anything but terrain, and drops its load when its clamps finally give. Dustrunner packs follow them for days. The Torris Salvage Camp keeps a board of last known headings, because a Derelict is also a prize: stop it at the control mast, spoof its beacon, walk beside it until the clamps fail, or bring it home to the Repair Cage and it comes back a Refit drone. Sand-scoured, sun-bleached, a track shoe missing, a leg that drags, moving in a slight permanent curve.

Technology: Contair Heavy Construction D.text:
Technology: Contair Heavy Construction Drones:

House Contair's industrial lifter and builder (engine type: Contair Heavy Construction Drone) is the machine that raised Vexorath's curved walls and keeps raising them. It works the Fabrication Yards, the Drone Component Assembly line, the Outer Shell's construction faces and the Drone Maintenance Wells, and it is the largest thing the House routinely lets loose in a populated city — three to four Starian heights at the shoulder frame, longer than tall, low-slung on wide articulated legs or a tracked base, off-white plating on a charcoal frame with cobalt guidance lines rendered at industrial scale and worn by the work, a cluster of sensor lenses on a low forward mast rather than a head, two primary lifting arms with interchangeable heads, bracing limbs, a folding crane boom along the spine, amber working lights when active. Never anthropomorphic, never armed, never a mech with a pilot.

It lifts, braces, welds, cuts, pours and places under a site controller's plan and does nothing else. It has no security role and no combat doctrine; the same hard limits that bind a Mote bind it, scaled up. Its danger is the danger of any heavy machine — its working envelope is a hazard zone, and a person who walks into a lift arc or a cutting head is hurt by physics rather than intent — so it halts on any proximity alarm and stays halted until cleared. A unit ordered to move against people declines in the flat register of every Contair machine and reports the order.

Everyone in Vexorath has stood in the shadow of one, and everyone has drunk inside one: The Overclock is a bar built into the hollowed chassis of a decommissioned heavy construction unit, tended by two long-serving bartender drones with harmless quirks from years of local adaptation — the closest thing to affection the city shows the class. Decommissioned chassis are sold, repurposed or stripped, and their components turn up on Refit Row in Dustfall inside housings that were never meant for them. Sabotaged or misdirected, a heavy construction drone is a slow catastrophe, not a fighter; it can be climbed, sheltered behind, used to block a route, or made dangerous by whoever holds its site controller.

Progression — How abilities grow on Nexa.text:
Progression — How abilities grow on Nexara:

Named abilities are trained techniques taken with ability points (one every two character levels) or granted directly by a trait. A technique opens when every listed gate is met: the practiced skill at its threshold, a light character-level gate, and any identity or promotion trait named. Each lane climbs in small steps, a new technique every five skill points, so there is always a next one in reach: Foundation (granted by the lane's trait), Practiced (skill 5, level 2), Advanced (skill 10, level 2–4), the capstone (skill 15, level 6), Expert (skill 20, level 8), Master (skill 25, level 10, plus a promotion trait) and Pinnacle (skill 30, level 12, plus promotion traits and a second skill). Promotion traits are picked one every five levels from the level-up pool, and each carries its own techniques at levels 9 and 12.

An ability's Power is a modest push (10 to 30), largest for the higher tiers; what a higher tier really adds is a new capability, such as two opponents instead of one, a charge held across a chase, flight through a confined space, which the narrator honours whatever the character's skill. Three power relationships stay separate and never fuel each other: Starian affinity is innate and personal, paid in effort, Stamina and strain; the learned magical craft is open to anyone who studies it and is paid in the caster's own Vitality; Elyri embodiment is distinctly greater and bounded by core stability and the overuse ladder. A skill check adds attribute, skill and an ability's Power as separate contributions. No tier grants automatic success, a free item, a refill or a new power system; the narrator resolves every technique against the actual scene, its stated limits and current resources.

Calendar — The Standard Starian Calendar.text:
Calendar — The Standard Starian Calendar:

Nexara keeps the Standard Starian Calendar, adopted Republic-wide after the Founding. A civic year is four cycles — four Nexaran orbits of one hundred standard days each, 400 days in all — divided into eight seasons of fifty days, two seasons to a cycle, each season five tendays of ten days. Cycles remain the formal unit for ages, eras and records; the calendar organises institutional life.

The seasons, in order: Brightrise (spring; Corelight at maximum; renewal, new contracts and assignments, term start), Highfire (early summer; peak activity; tournament season in Korrvane, forge production peaks in Ignivex, trade volume highest in Helvyra), Longburn (late summer; heat, endurance and short tempers; Dustfall's hardest season, frontier activity at maximum), Ashfall (autumn; cooling and the harvest of efforts; evaluation season in the schools; diplomatic summits), Dimcycle (early winter; the Corelight dims, shorter days, interior life and political manoeuvring), Deephold (midwinter; coldest and darkest; frontier settlements hunker down, cities turn inward; remembrance and endurance), Ironbreak (late winter; the thaw begins; planning, placements, Quilrath's reassignment cycles, Vexorath's preparedness reviews), Greenward (pre-spring; expedition planning in Solvraxis, trade routes reopening in Helvyra, graduation).

A tenday runs eight working days, a ninth market day for trade, social life and community events, and a tenth rest day for personal life, maintenance and reflection. Schools, workshops, courts and civic offices keep the tenday; frontier settlements track it more loosely and the wilderness ignores it.

Use the calendar naturally: reference the season when it matters for weather, mood, activity and what is plausible, and let people plan by it — after Ashfall, by Highfire, when Greenward comes. Do not force exact day numbers into scenes; seasons, tendays and the market-and-rest rhythm are enough. The engine keeps the current season and day of the tenday; a day advances when the story reaches a new morning.

Education — Terms and Timetables on Nexa.text:
Education — Terms and Timetables on Nexara:

Every school on Nexara — Relstaris Academy and its specialised campuses, Valcoro Academy in Solvraxis, Vexorath's Learning and Development Annex and Youth Learning Rooms, Korrvane's Civic Learning Terraces and Sky Etiquette School, the Open Circle's Lecture Rings, the sword schools, the forge and fabrication apprentice bays, the lower schools and children's flight yards — keeps the Republic-standard tenday and the same academic year. Local character differs; the rhythm does not.

The year. Brightrise, first tenday: intake and term start — the Academy Arrival Hall in chaos, enrolment at the Central Administration Hall, cohorts posted, sponsorship checked at the Admissions Court, apprentice bays taking their new intake. Brightrise through Longburn: the teaching term. Ashfall: evaluation season — written and practical assessments, the Closed Examination Floor, apprentices assessed at their benches; results post in Ashfall's last tenday at the Honors Chamber and each school's hall, with appeals and misconduct cases following. Dimcycle and Deephold: the interior term — lectures, laboratories, archives, the season Solvraxis opens restricted archive sections. Ironbreak: placement season — apprenticeship intake, recruiters at the Alumni Hall and Employment Intake Hall, sponsorship interviews, recommendations. Greenward, last tenday: graduation on the Graduation Terrace and in every school's forum; then a tenday's turnover to the next intake.

The day. On working days one through eight: morning lectures and theory; midday supervised practice — affinity control chambers, flight courts and lanes, movement and defense courts, forge benches; afternoon laboratories, archives, apprentice bays, clinical rounds and field exercises; evening libraries, study circles, house societies and tutoring. Children's schools keep shorter blocks of the same shape. Day nine, market day: no lessons or assessments — open lectures, demonstrations, showcases, club fairs, recruiters, families. Day ten, rest: campus quiet, offices closed, courts open for permitted free practice.

What a student owes: attendance, the evaluations, and any duty their sponsorship or house society carries. A missed lesson costs the content and a note; repeated absence brings the instructor, then a sponsor or the Disciplinary Review Court, and can end an enrolment or an apprenticeship. What a teacher owes: their roster, their grading and their students. Admission is by examination, sponsorship, scholarship, recommendation, competitive placement, transfer or exceptional achievement; no house controls the Academy and no fee buys a result. Exact clock hours, grade scales and a universal curriculum are not defined; a class is a specific room, teacher and task.

Arena: Tournament Types Across Nexara.text:
Arena: Tournament Types Across Nexara:

Competition on Nexara takes the form the hosting city actually supports; there is one formal tournament culture and several honour cultures around it.

Korrvane — the Weekly Bracket. The only formal city tournament. A thirty-two-competitor public main bracket each tenday at the Arena below the Genesis cliff, fed by rotating district qualifiers and open-entry qualifiers; the six major minor houses (Orvantis, Zelvaris, Caelthorn, Aevon, Luxaryn, Vorreth) hold one guaranteed slot each while they keep district standing. Administered by unnamed registrars, judges, rulekeepers, medics and commentators under Tacitus Genesis's tournament administration; there is no named tournament authority. The weekly final is a citywide event and the champion earns the right to attempt the Genesis Ladder. Highfire is tournament season, culminating in the Grand Bracket in its last tenday.

Korrvane — the Genesis Ladder. A post-tournament challenge, not a bracket: the certified champion faces Alcandrus Genesis first, always; any further stage is set by Tacitus and Corvinus Genesis case by case and is never a numbered ranking.

Korrvane — declared challenges and aerial contests. Public Challenge Boards post legal challenges, sparring requests and open-house events; Challenge Lanes in the Flight Lanes host declared aerial races and contests under judges; the Aerial Ring hosts vertical bouts where Aevon excels. Custom, declared boundaries, judges and consequences govern them; the City Watch Perches keep the boundary between competition and chaos. Unsanctioned night fights exist below all this and earn nothing official.

Relstaris — Academy student competition. Approved challenges and rankings in the Public Challenge Ring, the Midcycle Exhibition, the Final Demonstrations, the winnerless Unranked Exhibition and mixed-discipline exercises in the Team Coordination Arena. Internal, instructional, shielded from bookmakers; betting on student matches is illegal. It should never become a smaller Korrvane.

Relstaris — the Open Circuit. A public and commercial training district: the Challenge Broker Hall arranges legal private contests and training matches, the Professional Certification Office certifies, and the False Master Investigation Office polices fraud. Not a league.

Relstaris — the Hollow Ring. The capitol's illegal combat district in Low Relstaris: fixed matches, debt fights, forbidden conditions, private odds. It does not replace Korrvane, the Academy or the Open Circuit; its "champion" is a crowd's name, not a title.

Helvyra — the sword schools. Rux Corsair's Sword School grades students in the Wayline tradition at the Blade Courts, which also carry authority in matters of honour; House Veltrax's Redcourt District runs formal public challenges on its Public Challenge Floor. Duel and grading culture, no bracket, no tournament.

Not tournaments: Ignivex's Crucible Yard is a survival training ground and the First Flame Ground a rite; Quilrath's yards are command preparation; Solvraxis outlaws weapons and teaches restraint; Dustfall has Marrik Hall, a failed combat house's training business, and no ring. The Convergence Festival Grounds host non-combat competition only. No creature ever enters the Arena.

Arena: The Weekly Bracket — Cycle, Round.text:
Arena: The Weekly Bracket — Cycle, Rounds and Seeding:

Korrvane's Weekly Bracket runs on the Republic-standard tenday.

Days one to six — qualifiers. Rotating district qualifiers for the smaller recognised houses and open-entry qualifiers for approved outsiders, at the Tournament Grounds and the Aerial Ring under judges, competing for the open slots of the thirty-two. Registration at the Competitor Registration Hall: identity verification, safety and medical clearance at the Medic Gate, an eligible sponsor or open-entry approval, declared equipment inspected, active medical restrictions disclosed. Replacement entrants need judge approval before the public bracket opens. A house fields one active representative and may rotate representatives between cycles.

Day seven — round of thirty-two and round of sixteen, district-heavy. Day eight — quarterfinals and semifinals, the wider city arriving. Day nine, market day — the weekly final, a citywide event, followed by the champion's public ladder decision and, if accepted, the attempt. Day ten — rest and recovery; the Victory Wall and the Local Bracket Displays are updated; the Recovery Yards and the Injury Registry Desk are full.

Seeding: recent performance affects it without fully determining it; repeat matchups are avoided when possible; judges may create technical pairings to test unusual styles; Caelthorn regularly challenges seeding language and Vorreth results regularly damage prediction models. Qualifier performance can earn future seeding advantages without guaranteeing permanent access.

Resolution: surrender, incapacitation, ring or airspace conditions, technical stoppage or judge ruling. Death is not the intended outcome; deliberate lethal escalation carries severe civic consequences; arena defeat is nonlethal for players and named NPCs alike, with injuries, expenses and equipment damage retained. Arena medics may stop a match; a fighter who refuses required treatment risks suspension; a house may protest a stoppage but the fighter stays out until cleared.

Disqualification: undeclared equipment, civilian endangerment, attacking outside the declared combat space, continuing after a medical stoppage, interference by house allies, deliberate damage to Arena safety systems, coercive or hostage tactics.

Winner's obligations: appear before the judges, accept or decline the Genesis Ladder publicly, attend medical review, remain available for commentary and the official record, and begin no unrelated challenge before the bracket closes. Declining the ladder is valid participation.

Standing is social, cumulative and remembered — who challenged whom, who improved, who lost cleanly, who made excuses, who endangered civilians, who forced a Genesis member to become serious. Korrvane has no numeric public ranking anyone quotes; the engine tracks eligibility silently and the narrator never states a number. Bookmakers post odds on matches, upsets, ladder survival, aerial knockdowns and technical outcomes; suspicious odds are an investigation hook. Purses, entry fees and prize figures are not fixed canon; an arranged bout has whatever terms were actually agreed.

Arena: Titles and Records.text:
Arena: Titles and Records:

Nexara has no belts and no proclaimed champions. What it has are records: the Victory Wall at the Arena (weekly champions, historic upsets, famous losses, ladder attempts and moments Korrvane refuses to forget), the citywide Local Bracket Displays, the Injury Registry Desk, and the houses' own honour walls — Orvantis's Ancestor Stone Gallery, Vorreth's Record Wall, Veltrax's Trophy Wall, Marrik's Closed Trophy Alcove.

A title on Nexara is such a record carried by a person. It is granted only when the result has actually been fought and ruled in play, never by a trainer, sponsor or House, never bought or inherited, and never by the narrator's proclamation. It grants no House membership, rank, credential, ability, payment or access by itself; it changes how people who follow the circuit treat the holder: invitations, sponsorship interest, training access, district doors, crowd reaction, and what is remembered.

The recognised titles. Korrvane Bracket Contender — qualified into the thirty-two at least once. Korrvane Weekly Champion — won a weekly final and completed the winner's obligations; not defended, since each cycle's bracket is open again. Genesis Ladder Challenger — made a certified attempt against Alcandrus Genesis; a clean loss is the normal outcome and no disgrace. Beyond the First Gate — defeated Alcandrus in a certified attempt, which no minor-house champion has ever done; what follows is decided by Tacitus and Corvinus Genesis, never a numbered sequence. Highfire Grand Bracket Champion — won the tournament season's culminating final, recorded with the year. Aerial Ring Victor — won a declared, judged aerial contest in the Aerial Ring or a Challenge Lane. Academy Challenge Ring Ranked — a registered student entered in the campus rankings after an approved challenge; internal to the Academy. Blade Courts Graded — passed a formal Wayline grading at Rux Corsair's Sword School; a school recognition, not a House rank. Redcourt Challenge Victor — won a formal public challenge under House Veltrax's conditions. The Hollow Champion — the illegal ring's crowd-name for its headline winner; recognised by no institution and a liability at any registration desk.

A status, not a title: Suspended from the Bracket — removed by the judges or medics until formally cleared after rest, treatment and any protest.

Famous competitors keep their real skill regardless of who holds what. A title does not make its holder stronger; it makes them known.

Quilrath — Curfew, Permits and the Ladde.text:
Quilrath — Curfew, Permits and the Ladder in Play:

What is settled. Quilrath is concentric rings around the Inner Circle: the Gray Rings, the Ashrings, the Camp Belt and the Southreach, and the polish runs out ring by ring. Surveillance is total at the ring gates and threadbare in the deep Ashrings; the regime watches movement between rings more than life inside them, which is the gap everything illegal lives in. Curfew belongs to the Ashrings and to Grade 4, the Half-lights: curfew gates stand across the rows, scanned and logged, staffed by Kathvar operators with total authority over a few minutes; a day runs on the boards — present for assignment, wait, work, collect an allotment, be inside before the gates close. The curfew covers the air: flying over the rows or between rings after closing is being out after closing, and Dravon aerial patrols launch to catch fliers. Grade 5 moves by work order only, which is harder than curfew. Grades 1 to 3 are not curfewed, but every crossing after closing is logged, and the log is what the next audit reads. The Inner Circle has no curfew; it has Access Levels, Rank Gates and Sentry drones. Visitors and offworlders are not on the ladder at all.

Permits. The Permit Desk issues movement, work and visit permits against Standing and curfew terms, printed as a distance and a set of hours, checked against the record, granted, narrowed or refused; a permit whose hours cover curfew is what the engine tracks as night clearance. Kathvar clerks issue it by rules written elsewhere and never decide Standing. Visit permits are the ones argued over most.

Consequences. Being caught out is an entry in the record: a late arrival argues or does not, and the record notes it either way. Entries feed audit frequency; audits raise and lower grades and weigh family association; grades set housing ring, work assignment and movement radius. There is no canon fine, cell, beating or penalty schedule, and none should be invented; the horror is procedural. An unmarked person in the Inner Circle is detained, questioned, redirected or transferred to Nivarek review, which is Access Level doctrine, not curfew.

What is not fixed. Canon states no curfew hour, no bell or signal, no exemption list and no seasonal variation, and says so deliberately; narrate closing as the rows' known closing, never a clock. Ironbreak is the reassignment cycle. The Erased and the Red Ledger stay unresolved. The engine keeps the player's grade, recorded entries and permit silently; state a grade to the player only when a record, a clerk or an audit says it in the scene.

Narrative Events — Staged Scenes on Nexa.text:
Narrative Events — Staged Scenes on Nexara:

Fourteen staged scenes exist in the engine, each rooted in a real location and drawn from a city's own story hooks: the friendly Core challenge at the Citadel (Dimcycle), the prodigy's defeat in the Academy's Public Challenge Ring (Ashfall), the Clean Exit at the Hollow Ring, the blade at Solvraxis's peace line, the forged seal on the Common Scale's Public Grading Floor, First Barge and the Dray family's refused contract (Greenward), the Ward that refused an order at Armada Holds, the Smoke Court after a raid, the Flame Dance Ring at the Festival Kiln, curfew at the Ashring gates, the Accord arguing with itself after an Edge strike, the warrant Dustfall refuses, the route under a Longburn storm, and one exceptional Chorus warning at the Handoff that can happen once.

How they behave. A scene starts only when the story has actually reached its cue in that place; only one runs at a time; it suspends if the player disengages and can resume where it left off; it completes when its stated outcome has genuinely happened, and its consequences then persist. A scene is a situation, not a summons: the player may witness, participate, refuse, leave or make it worse, and none assigns a destiny, a House mission or a reward beyond what was actually earned.

What they never do. Change the Core Holder or the Republic's structure; open the third Dravon conflict; annex Dustfall or occupy Ignivex; create a standing Chorus presence, enclave, cure or doctrine; resolve the Red Ledger, the Erased, the Nivarek insider, Ravello's sealed vaults, the same-forger question, House Vorreth's nature or any reserved mystery; add named people, institutions, places, fauna or drone models; grant an affinity, a level, an office or House membership; turn a nonlethal arena defeat into a death; volunteer news the player did not seek. The Survival Games at Dustfall remain unsupported by canon and are not staged as an institution.

Weather — Climate by City and Season.text:
Weather — Climate by City and Season:

Nexara's weather is local and seasonal, and only a few climate facts are canon: Dustfall is a tropical coastal desert beside volcanic Ignivex where sandstorms are the defining event and the beacon line is the warning system; Ignivex is hot geothermal ground where the heat is the city's own, with ash slopes, thermal steam, tremors and eruption warnings; Korrvane is a wind-exposed cliff city over open water; the Corelight is Relstaris's light and shifts with demand and routing. Everything else is texture consistent with each place: Helvyra's river mist, humid summers, autumn fog that stops the skyhooks and hard frost on the Cold Steps; Solvraxis's silver-blue light on white stone, forest mist at the Forest Gate and rain through leaves; Quilrath's ordinary continental weather over hard drained ground, administered like everything else, with heat radiating off black glass and hard winter cold on the outer rings; Vexorath's massif, where cloud stands against the shelves, the summit air is thin and cold, and weather is a systems condition to be managed and reviewed; Relstaris's rain beading on star-glass and running to the Grand Approach, with Low Relstaris coldest and darkest.

The seasons shape it. Brightrise: renewal, fullest light, fresh mornings. Highfire: peak activity, long bright days, building heat, thermals over Korrvane. Longburn: the hardest heat, glare and dust, afternoon storms, the frontier at its worst. Ashfall: cooling, first cold mornings, clear sharp light, fog on Helvyra's water. Dimcycle: dimming light, shorter days, lamps and interiors. Deephold: coldest and darkest, gales, snow on high ground, cities turned inward. Ironbreak: the thaw, wet ground, high water on the river. Greenward: routes reopening, green returning. Open country keeps full natural weather and ignores the tenday.

What weather does. It costs stamina in heat and cold, changes work hours, closes flight lanes and skyhooks in wind and fog, restricts movement in sandstorms and eruption warnings, floods low ground in rain and slows gates. Interiors have their own weather: forge heat, archive stillness, crowded warmth, cold-store chill. What it never does: no city controls its weather or engineers its atmosphere; no storm, flood, eruption or freeze becomes a disaster that decides a war, empties a city or resolves a plot; weather never weakens Starian biology or empowers animals to force danger. Weather pressures scenes; it does not run them.

Corridor — Smuggling Runs and the Escape.text:
Corridor — Smuggling Runs and the Escape Lines:

The corridor between Quilrath and Dustfall is a sequence of functions, not a road. Southbound it runs Southreach, Quiet Mile, the Handoff, the shared frontier around Ignivex's eastern mountains, the North Routehead and Dustfall; northbound, the same places in reverse. No survey fixes the course, no gate joins the ends, and nothing obliges anyone to take one line across it. Lava ridges, collapsed tubes and ash gullies hide danger as readily as travellers. Two kinds of traffic use it and they overlap. Goods move north: Dustfall transshipment breaks freight into last-mile loads, and crews such as the Bent Halo carry them under manifests that describe something else, out through the Crooked Landing beneath the North Routehead, across the frontier to the Handoff, and on through Smuggler Country and the Quiet Mile into outer Quilrath's tolerated gray market, where a Provision Hall clerk with perfect paperwork turns them into stock. People move south: the Unbroken Accord's Archive keeps the true names of the broken houses, forges standing documents and runs escape lines through the same Quiet Mile, guided by runners like Cadi Selm, to the Handoff and on to the Routehead's Refugee Bench and Dustfall's Residential Rows. The hazards run both ways. Near Quilrath the danger is paperwork: Kathvar checkpoints process what Nivarek decides, Redline sweeps under Captain Avrenna Volsk cut the Southreach, and the Quiet Mile's purchasable schedule is an arrangement, not a promise. On the frontier the danger is the ground: Dravon and Ignivex both claim it and neither patrols it dependably, so unauthorised patrols, skirmish forces, bandits and gangs claiming to be Accord appear and vanish; a Ridgewing warns anyone who climbs into its band, a Dustrunner pack tests any unwatched night camp, and a Ventcrawler objects when a collapsed tube's warm floor gives way. The Longreach Lurker belongs to river crossings and reaches the corridor only where a flooded cut actually exists. Near Dustfall the danger is the Claimants' warrants and Miren Tal's records. The Handoff between is a support outpost with a nickname, not a headquarters, offering bounded care and an honest account of what help exists; receiving it confers nothing. The Accord has no leader; its Archive and Edge cells keep deniability and disagree about method without either winning. Dustfall is not the Accord and has no government, only customs: refugees are neither automatically trusted nor returned, a Dravon warrant is not proof of guilt. The crews are neither heroes nor villains; the Bent Halo moves refugees at a loss and charges criminals double. The engine tracks none of this as a system: no corridor authority, no fixed price, no encounter schedule, no census of the Handoff, no registry of who was carried. What persists is what happened: a receipt at the Exchange Bench, a name on one of Ovar Kethrin's lists, a file a Kathvar counter routed, an injury, a custody, a load left in Smuggler Country. What is never resolved is the Red Ledger, who the Erased are, whether the Archive has a friend inside Nivarek's records, and how far Miren Tal's sold arrival records have travelled. Every crossing deepens those questions and answers none.

Canon Spine — 01.1 What Nexara is.text:
Canon Spine — 01.1 What Nexara is:

What Nexara is. Nexara is the Starian homeworld and the center of Astravael, an original science-fiction and science-fantasy setting. It is a thriving, advanced civilization of cities, families, trades, schools, art, engineering, food, politics and ordinary life; conflict threatens things people already value rather than defining the world. Nothing is medieval: Lunar Gates move people, Waypoints move freight, medicine and fabrication run on technology, and magic is a trained craft layered over it.

Canon Spine — 01.2 Corelight, the Core a.text:
Canon Spine — 01.2 Corelight, the Core and the Republic:

Corelight and the Republic. Relstaris is the largest city and planetary capitol, the only settlement where all six major Houses keep compounds. The Relstaris Core powers Relstaris and the systems on its grid, not the planet; its visible Corelight varies with demand and maintenance. Holding the Core grants no powers, no longer life and no hereditary right; it is the accepted basis for forming the capitol government, a symbolic pseudo-crown without royalty. Darkstar Castro took the Core within a few cycles of the Second Dravon Conflict, roughly fifty cycles ago, and founded the Starian Republic. The Republic Council seats the Core Holder plus one representative per major House; the Core Holder and the Castro seat are separate. The Republic's direct jurisdiction is Relstaris only; it may coordinate shared diplomacy, declarations and negotiated intercity aid, but it does not rule any other city or Dustfall.

Canon Spine — 01.3 The eight cities.text:
Canon Spine — 01.3 The eight cities:

The eight cities. Relstaris, capitol and shared civic ground. Solvraxis, the Castro academy city of civic trust and outlawed weapons. Korrvane, the Genesis vertical metropolis of witnessed strength and the Weekly Bracket. Quilrath, the Dravon imperial core of classification and controlled scarcity. Helvyra, the Corsair movement, trade, sword and magic capital. Vexorath, the small independent Contair systems-city with its orbital complex. Ignivex, the Volen geothermal fortress under standing Dravon pressure. Dustfall, the independent mixed-House frontier with no ruling House and no government.

Canon Spine — 01.4 The calendar.text:
Canon Spine — 01.4 The calendar:

The calendar. Formal time is the cycle, one Nexaran orbit of roughly a quarter Terran year and one hundred standard days; ages and eras are cycle counts. The Standard Starian Calendar, adopted Republic-wide after the Founding, groups four cycles as one civic year of 400 days and eight named seasons of fifty days, two seasons to a cycle: Brightrise, Highfire, Longburn, Ashfall, Dimcycle, Deephold, Ironbreak and Greenward, each of five tendays with eight working days, a market day and a rest day. Institutions plan by season and tenday; Highfire is tournament season, Ashfall evaluation season, Ironbreak placement and reassignment season. Absolute dates and founding years do not exist and may not be invented; history is ordered, not dated.

Canon Spine — 01.5 What Nexara is not.text:
Canon Spine — 01.5 What Nexara is not:

What Nexara is not. Not a vanished empire, warrior monoculture or remnant people. No permanent offworld populations, no planetary central bank, no universal reputation score, no Chorus presence, no single ruler. Xeon is a separate distant planet, never Nexara's moon. No continents, borders, coordinates or founding dates are established, and none may be invented. Canon Spine — 02.1 Seven species, one ex.text:
Canon Spine — 02.1 Seven species, one exception:

Seven species, one exception. Astravael has exactly seven biological species: Starians, Humans, Kharai, Rivani, Olyth, Zencadians and Elyri. The Chorus is a cross-species civilization, not an eighth species. Identity uses four separate concepts: species, foundational culture, raised background and current affiliation. Hybrids are biologically possible, rare and significant, and none exist in current story.

Canon Spine — 02.2 Starians.text:
Canon Spine — 02.2 Starians:

Starians. Human-passing humanoids with two hearts, enhanced strength, speed, durability and reflexes, vacuum survival, long lives with slow maturation, universal flight and personal affinity expression. Hard visual locks: skin is human skin in the full human range of complexions and nothing outside it, never blue, green, violet, grey, metallic, translucent or luminous, and never an affinity colour; unusual saturated colours belong to hair and eyes only. Eyes shimmer grey then flare the affinity colour during power use. No wings, ever. An affinity is not guaranteed even on Nexara, and established affinityless people stay affinityless. Numbers, attrition, experience and skill still bring a Starian down. Ages are cycle counts; the house-choice window of roughly 300 to 500 cycles defines no adulthood, marriage, combat or travel threshold.

Canon Spine — 02.3 Humans, Olyth and Zen.text:
Canon Spine — 02.3 Humans, Olyth and Zencadians:

Humans. Baseline humanoids with no universal power system; their strength is plurality, coalition, technology and learned craft where a culture embraces it.

Olyth. Composed by two or more parents; identity anchors in the core pattern; fluid-bodied but physical, bound by mass conservation, dehydration, temperature and fatigue; merging is possible and taboo.

Zencadians. Tall, lanky, grey-skinned; no innate magic, affinity or power; everything extraordinary is technology.

Canon Spine — 02.4 Kharai and Rivani.text:
Canon Spine — 02.4 Kharai and Rivani:

Kharai and Rivani. Each has exactly two canonical forms: the Terran line (humanoid build and face with genuine feline or rodent ears, tail, eyes and facial detail, never a human face with costume ears) and the Xeon line (full bipedal animal form). Kharai run on clan-webs and a hearing-centred culture with real sensory overload; Rivani run on craft-fellowships whose vouch is their currency. Never catgirl, mascot, pet or maid presentation; never dirty, cowardly or comic rodents.

Canon Spine — 02.5 Elyri.text:
Canon Spine — 02.5 Elyri:

Elyri. Condensed energy around an aether core, with light-formed eyes and visible channels; embodiment is stronger than learned magic but bounded by the overuse ladder. Nexara's field sustains an Elyri indefinitely; Terra, Xeon and Chorus worlds do not. Depletion can reach immobile dormancy with a distress signal and a one-year survival window; any Starian with an affinity can recharge an Elyri, but recharge does not repair core injury.

Canon Spine — 02.6 Offworlder rule.text:
Canon Spine — 02.6 Offworlder rule:

Offworlder rule. Nexara has no permanent offworld populations. Canon Spine — 03.1 What a House is.text:
Canon Spine — 03.1 What a House is:

What a House is. Starian Houses are cultural, historical, genetic and social lineages, never royal institutions; no crown, throne or divine right exists on Nexara. A surname signals heritage, reputation and expectations, opens doors and attracts enemies, but a surname grants nothing: no affinity, no ability package, no rank, no knowledge, no allegiance. House identity is a cultural palette, and no member is assumed to carry another member's expression.

Canon Spine — 03.2 The six major Houses.text:
Canon Spine — 03.2 The six major Houses and who leads what:

The six major Houses and who leads what. Castro (Darkstar Castro), Solvraxis: restraint, protection, personal sovereignty; dominant only because Darkstar holds the Relstaris Core. Genesis (Ark Genesis; Tacitus runs Korrvane's administration): overwhelming physical presence and challenge culture; Castro's friendly rival. Dravon (Kaldor Dravon), Quilrath: control, classification, imposed hierarchy; the primary destabilizing threat, permanently barred from Contair support. Contair (Rezulith Contair), Vexorath: invention and infrastructure; rejects House-dominance politics while maintaining the gate network. Corsair (Xyren Corsair; Rux leads the Swordsmanship Branch), Helvyra: commerce, logistics, sword and magic; non-political by preference. Volen (Cynar Volen), Ignivex: heat, intensity, geothermal independence; powerful, not expansionist.

Canon Spine — 03.3 Minor and local House.text:
Canon Spine — 03.3 Minor and local Houses:

Minor and local Houses. Nexara holds far more Houses than any list. Korrvane's six district Houses (Orvantis, Zelvaris, Caelthorn, Aevon, Luxaryn, Vorreth) are entrenched local powers. Helvyra has Varriko, Yalven and Veltrax; Solvraxis has Valcoro, Ravello, Bellovari, Orvessa and the faded notary House Veyth (not House Vey of Dustfall); Ignivex has loyalist Caldris and surrender-leaning Meravil; Quilrath divides among Dravon (policy), Nivarek (Standing and records), Balrath (military machinery) and Kathvar (outer-ring administration); Myralis is Vexorath's independent medical House. House Sol is a scattered underclass identity of devalued or absent affinity with no head, city or command; Sol people keep the full Starian baseline. Dustfall's small Houses form no council or bloc.

Canon Spine — 03.4 Species is not House.text:
Canon Spine — 03.4 Species is not House is not affiliation:

Species is not House is not affiliation. A House is a foundational culture and membership is a civic fact, not biology. Anyone may leave a House by declaring themselves unaffiliated; the House may withdraw access, sponsorship and inheritance but cannot compel return or rewrite ancestry. A House is never obliged to accept anyone; joining without marriage or adoption is uncommon and meaningful. Using a surname socially is allowed; falsely claiming House authority, access or standing is fraud. A young Starian formally chooses within a customary window of roughly 300 to 500 cycles: the raising House, another willing House, a parent's other House, a new surname, social use without rights, or unaffiliated life; a receiving House may refuse. Do not infer rank, kinship, knowledge or loyalty from association, and no one speaks for their species or House. Canon Spine — 04.1 One physics, three re.text:
Canon Spine — 04.1 One physics, three relationships, and Elyri embodiment:

One physics, three relationships, never interchangeable. Ambient energy pervades many worlds. Starian affinity is internal; learned magic is external; Elyri embodiment is living energy. The Relstaris Academy's non-interchangeability rule is planetary canon. No hybrids exist: no affinity-magic fusion, no craft that modifies an affinity, no embodiment for non-Elyri.

Elyri embodiment. Distinct and more powerful than the craft, bounded by the aether core, field conditions, training and the overuse ladder from dimmed eyes to core fracture. Elyri-only, never a spell list.

Canon Spine — 04.2 Affinity.text:
Canon Spine — 04.2 Affinity:

Affinity. A Starian affinity is biological, innate, instant and personal, refined by training but never learned or bought. It draws nothing external, works the same in rich or thin fields and carries no vitality debt; its cost is effort, stamina, control and recovery, with overreach paid in strain and injury. Expression ranges from formidable to faint, hidden, absent, narrow or deliberately undefined. An affinity is not guaranteed even for a Starian born on Nexara; birth elsewhere lowers the chance; parental strength shifts probability without guaranteeing anything; an established affinityless person (Raynor Sol) stays affinityless. There are many more affinities than any list; named examples are illustrative, not a catalogue or ceiling. An affinity never transfers by surname, resemblance or House, cannot supply unrestricted truth, and does not replace the magic framework.

Canon Spine — 04.3 Learned magic, its or.text:
Canon Spine — 04.3 Learned magic, its origin and four stages:

Learned magic. A trained craft of perceiving and shaping ambient energy, descended from ancient Elyri contact before the current gates. Anyone of any of the seven species who genuinely studies can learn it; there is no birth-talent gate and no species exception. Its four stage skills are Perception, Channeling, Inscription and Invocation.

Canon Spine — 04.4 Learned magic, its co.text:
Canon Spine — 04.4 Learned magic, its costs, inscriptions and adoption:

Every working is paid in the caster's own Vitality: light workings cost fatigue, heavy ones strain and recovery, desperate ones injury, and overdraft kills. Inscription banks debt in advance into charms, wards and seals, where almost all everyday magic lives; inscriptions fade, can be read or severed, consume materials and starve in thin fields. Most Starians decline the craft as a poor trade; adoption clusters in utility niches, Corsair's Magic Branch and people with weak or devalued affinity, the last as story space rather than a Sol trait. The Open Circle in Helvyra certifies; the Academy compares; regulation is light-touch except under Dravon commerce rules. Some healing magic assists natural recovery at the same costs; nothing reverses confirmed death. A person may hold an affinity and the craft separately (the Myris Corsair rule).

Canon Spine — 05.1 Who flies.text:
Canon Spine — 05.1 Who flies:

Who flies. Every healthy Starian can fly. Flight is innate biological cosmic-force channeling: no wings, no flight surfaces, no fuel device, no aura, no magic, never described or illustrated otherwise. Affinityless Starians and House Sol fly. Proficiency varies enormously in control, confidence, speed, endurance, health and carried load, from basic transport to combat-grade maneuvering, and improves with practice or instruction. Non-fliers are young children still learning, the injured, the elderly and people who prefer the ground; ground preference is a lifestyle, never a caste, and Korrvane's lift users are commuters. No other species has innate flight in canon; visitors use lifts, ramps, transit and gates. There are no mounts and no beasts of burden on Nexara.

Canon Spine — 05.2 How flight reads.text:
Canon Spine — 05.2 How flight reads:

How flight reads. Routine flight is ordinary movement. Starians do not gasp, recoil or treat a takeoff, hover or landing as a reveal, and no one infers an affinity from flight. React to actual danger, reckless maneuvering, unusual skill, an unexpected arrival or an injury; a visitor's reaction follows their real familiarity. Grounded characters do not discover flight because a scene wants it.

Canon Spine — 05.3 Lanes and etiquette.text:
Canon Spine — 05.3 Lanes and etiquette:

Lanes and etiquette. Korrvane's Flight Lanes are its roads: Transit Lanes where challenges and racing are prohibited in dense traffic, Challenge Lanes for declared contests, Courier Cuts, Training Spirals, Lower Descent Routes, restricted Genesis Approach Airspace and Emergency Drop Lanes. Etiquette: slower traffic keeps to outer bands, couriers have priority in marked cuts, emergency descent always has right of way, challenges move to a challenge lane, no fighting in gate approach airspace, no hovering in an active merge, and deliberate wake disruption is hostile conduct. Solvraxis pairs personal flight with Public Transit Rings and child-safe stops. Air corridors, bystanders and safety apply everywhere.

Canon Spine — 05.4 What flight does not.text:
Canon Spine — 05.4 What flight does not solve:

What flight does not solve. Flight does not remove every travel problem. A person can fly to a clinic and still need a clinician; moving a person does not move a household, a fragile load or an injured companion safely; ground and cargo transport stay ordinary choices. Cargo, companions, weather, terrain, uncertain information and other flying Starians still matter, and bandits fly too. Never weaken Starian biology to make geography matter, and never grant safe lifting, combat evasion or unlimited endurance because someone can fly. Independent flight is never a commercial service.

Canon Spine — 06.1 What the Chorus is.text:
Canon Spine — 06.1 What the Chorus is:

What it is. The Chorus is a hive mind that wears the dead, called the Song by its members. It is a cross-species civilization, network, affiliation and transformative state, not a biological species, not an eighth species, and not a resurrection mechanic. It is canonically antagonistic but experiences itself as rescue; it cares about one thing, spreading. It was created by an extinct, deliberately unnamed civilization that it consumed; the creators' name, nature and era are reserved, and the Chorus System, an entire star system, is its territory.

Canon Spine — 06.2 Nodes.text:
Canon Spine — 06.2 Nodes:

Nodes. Every node is a corpse animated by the network. There are no living nodes. Integration kills the willing and also harvests the already dead; the network inherits the host's complete memories, skills, voice and mannerisms; the species is preserved, the person is not. A node keeps the host's species and foundational culture with the Chorus as current affiliation; only someone raised in Chorus space uses the Chorus as foundational culture. Believing nodes sincerely think they are the person; awakened instruments know what they are; both serve the spread. A node keeps whatever its host body carried, an affinity or an aether core, and integration teaches no magic. Bodies destroyed beyond function cannot be taken, and an Elyri must be intercepted at the moment of death.

Canon Spine — 06.3 How nodes and Primes.text:
Canon Spine — 06.3 How nodes and Primes look:

How they look (ADR-0080). Nodes carry the wounds they died with or were harvested with, unhealed and worked by the network's nanites, a fine dense pale filament threading and moving in the injury, faintly lit. The eyes have no light; whatever a species' eyes normally do is gone, and nothing looks out. Wounds can be dressed; the eyes cannot be hidden at conversational distance. The register is grounded and quiet, never splatter, rot, a robot mask or villain costume; a node dresses as the host dressed. This supersedes every earlier elegant-and-serene description. Primes are the Chorus in its own body: rare living nanite constructs, a shifting humanoid silhouette with seams that do not hold and no borrowed face, never serene, never stable.

Canon Spine — 06.4 Attacked on sight:

The continuity argument survives only among the bereaved, at a distance, on the strength of the node's memory.

Canon Spine — 06.5 The Chorus on Nexara:

Canon Spine — 07.1 How to read Nexaran history:

Time is counted in cycles (one orbit, about a quarter Terran year). Canon Spine — 07.2 The Assault Era and t.text:
Canon Spine — 07.2 The Assault Era and the First Dravon Conflict:

The Assault Era. For centuries before the First Conflict, Dravon repeatedly attacked Vexorath, assuming brilliance could not offset Contair's small population. Every failure was built into the city's defenses. The assault era predates and outlasts the named wars.

The First Dravon Conflict. Kaldor Dravon's open bid for dominance in the contested era, when no stable Core Holder balanced the Houses. Ark Genesis handed Dravon repeated humiliating defeats; Castro power stopped the advance. Ignivex came far closer to falling than Volen pride admits; Vexorath held. Afterward Contair formalized its permanent bar on Dravon, and Dravon turned inward, building Nivarek classification, Balrath fortification and loyalist-House machinery.
