Canon Spine — 07.3 The Interbellum and t.text:
Canon Spine — 07.3 The Interbellum and the Second Dravon Conflict:

The Interbellum. Dravon expanded by absorption: small Houses such as Vaereth, Nhalor, Edras and Sorn were broken through recruitment, forced service, confiscation and disappearances. Raids on Ignivex resumed and never stopped. Refugee flight toward Dustfall became permanent.

The Second Dravon Conflict. The great war within living memory, the one every city means by "the war". Helvyra front: Torvex Corsair died, passing Commerce and eventually House leadership to his son Xyren, and the postwar Dravon Disconnection severed all direct Helvyra to Dravon links. Ignivex front: the Great Raid killed Serava Volen at Soren Dravon's hand. Korrvane front: Sorvina Genesis's parents died and Ark raised her; the Dravon Scar Path keeps the memory. Vexorath front: Dravon's last conventional campaigns failed and Lumina Reach's completion closed the siege age. Dravon withdrew without surrender: no treaty, no reparations, no accountability.

Canon Spine — 07.4 Aftermath, the present, and settled versus reserved:

Aftermath and present. Within a few cycles Darkstar Castro took the Relstaris Core and founded the Starian Republic, approximately fifty cycles ago. The peace is real and post-war; nobody calls it settled. Dravon's Red War Room plans a third conflict against Ignivex, Dustfall, Relstaris and offworld targets while standing pressure continues.

Canon Spine — 09.1 The hard rule of gates and orbit:

Canon Spine — 09.2 Who moves what: trave.text:
Canon Spine — 09.2 Who moves what: travelers and freight:

Who moves what. Lunar Gates move travelers, built by generations of Contair engineering; one House maintaining the transit spine is a standing political fact. Personal effects, mobility aids and bounded traveler-accompanied courier consignments ride with a passenger; routine commercial stock and bulk supplies are freight, handled through Corsair Waypoints and the wider logistics system, and a cargo space beside a Gate proves no freight service. Waypoints are Corsair logistics on Contair architecture: sorting, authentication, storage, courier dispatch and settlement supply, present in every major settlement except Quilrath.

Canon Spine — 09.3 Routes that exist.text:
Canon Spine — 09.3 Routes that exist:

Routes that exist. Relstaris holds the Grand Lunar Gate Hub, the largest shared passenger interchange. Helvyra holds one of the few major hubs. Korrvane's distributed plazas link to Relstaris, Solvraxis and Helvyra. Ignivex connects only to Relstaris and Dustfall. Quilrath has exactly one old Contair-built gate, to Relstaris, kept barely working by Dravon engineers without Contair support; there is no direct Helvyra to Dravon Waypoint or gate link (the Dravon Disconnection), and Helvyra to Relstaris and Relstaris to Quilrath are separately permitted journeys with no through-clearance. Dustfall's patched gate works intermittently to Relstaris, Ignivex and Helvyra with no official gatekeeper. No other links, distances, coordinates or travel times are established.

Canon Spine — 09.4 The frontier corridor.text:
Canon Spine — 09.4 The frontier corridor:

The frontier. Ignivex lies between Quilrath and Dustfall; the smuggling route runs around Ignivex's eastern mountains, not through the city, in the sequence Southreach, Quiet Mile, the separate Accord outpost (the Handoff), the shared eastern-Ignivex encounter space, North Routehead, Dustfall. This is functional progression, not a surveyed road. Competing Dravon and Ignivex claims and skirmishes prevent dependable patrols; cover shelters danger as readily as travelers; unfamiliar territory does not automatically contain an ambush. Canon Spine — 10.1 Credit and prices.text:
Canon Spine — 10.1 Credit and prices:

Credit. The Nexaran Credit is fully digital, accepted throughout Nexara and in parts of Xeon; exchange rates and Xeon locations are reserved. No coinage, currency abbreviation, central bank, offline mechanism or reputation score exists. Goods and services have costs everywhere, including water, power, meals, lodging, rides, repairs, classes and clinical care. Each city has its own accepted baseline in Credits, differing by category rather than one multiplier: a simple meal about 4 to 7, a modest room-night 14 to 28, an ordinary completed shift 45 to 85 and a skilled shift 105 to 195, with Korrvane cheapest, Vexorath paying best, Quilrath squeezed (an authorized Gray Rings basket of three meals, a room and utilities costs 49 against a 45 shift) and Dustfall cheap to sleep in but costly to supply. These are anchors, not tariffs; the actual provider, item and circumstances govern a quote. Barter, sponsorship, allotments, institutional issue and personal obligation coexist with Credit.

Canon Spine — 10.3 The tenday, food and housing:

Canon Spine — 11.1 Defeat is not death;.text:
Canon Spine — 11.1 Defeat is not death; famous competitors keep their skill:

Defeat is not death. Arena and arranged-fight defeat is nonlethal for players and named NPCs alike: the match ends by its stopping conditions and leads to treatment, with injuries, expenses and equipment damage retained. Ordinary combat defeat continues through context-supported capture, rescue or hospital care, narrated as incapacitation or critical injury, never a death quietly reversed. Play continues through the same character record; only actual Chorus integration is a canonical death. Most named-NPC defeats preserve the person through withdrawal, surrender or plausible House or faction rescue; lethal circumstances remain possible outside arenas, and confirmed death is never undone.

Famous competitors keep their real skill. No opponent weakens to guarantee a player's victory, generic criminals never receive a named NPC's power, and named champions keep their established capability regardless of who holds what. A title does not make its holder stronger; it makes them known.

Canon Spine — 11.2 The Weekly Bracket in.text:
Canon Spine — 11.2 The Weekly Bracket in brief:

The Weekly Bracket in brief. Korrvane's Arena runs the only formal city tournament: a thirty-two-competitor public bracket each tenday under Tacitus Genesis's administration. Qualifiers run days one to six, the bracket days seven and eight, the final on market day nine; the six district Houses hold one guaranteed slot each; registration needs verification, medical clearance, a sponsor or open-entry approval and inspected equipment. The champion publicly accepts or declines the Genesis Ladder, where Alcandrus Genesis is always first and no minor-House champion has ever passed him; further stages are set case by case by Tacitus and Corvinus, never a numbered ranking. Standing is social; the narrator never states a number. Titles are records granted only when a result was fought and ruled in play, never by narrator, trainer, sponsor or House, and confer no membership, rank, ability or payment; the ten recognised titles run from Bracket Contender to the unrecognised Hollow Champion. No belts, weight classes, fixed purses or minimum ages exist. No creature enters the Arena.

Canon Spine — 12.2 Player choice, offers.text:
Canon Spine — 12.2 Player choice, offers and news:

Player choice belongs to the player. Never supply the player's unspoken thoughts, dialogue, feelings, consent or next action; stop at a meaningful response point. An offer is not acceptance, a possible reward is not a paid reward, and interest is not consent to a job; create no accepted quest, cost or failed journal entry because an NPC proposed something. For an accepted quest, independent completion by others is failure while meaningful contribution counts as success.

Knowledge and news. Knowledge belongs to particular people and travels through actual channels. News is player-initiated in every mode: screens and slates may exist, but no bulletins, teasers, overheard headlines or companion recitations are volunteered, and reading news accepts nothing.

Relstaris: Everyday Operations.text:
A Relstaris working day is read off the Corelight. Shift workers cross South Relstaris on lifts, transit rings and the slow public flight corridors before the light reaches Peak, because fast flight is restricted in dense civic corridors and the Public Flight Crossing backs up by the time Academy students arrive late. The tenday runs eight working days, a market day and a rest day, and the Grand Market and the Worker Food Court are loudest on the ninth. A simple meal costs about 5 Credits at the Cheap Food Terrace, a modest room-night about 26 with 2 more for utilities, a short paid ride 3; an ordinary completed shift pays around 70 and a skilled one around 150, and the actual employer sets the quote. Work is found at the Open Contract Hall, on the Public Job Floor and the Immediate Work Queue, or through a Capitol Service term that pays a living wage and opens subsidised mid-city housing without conferring rank or credential. A consequential job is fixed before it starts: client, task, competence, period, pay, materials and access. An offer is not acceptance, and walking out of the Hall creates no contract. At Fade the Nexaran Table fills, Starfall opens, and the Night Transit Walk carries the late shift home under Low.

Relstaris: Signs and Membership.text:
In the capitol you read belonging off buildings before people. The six major Houses keep compounds on the Grand House Concourse, and a banner raised or dropped a few metres along Hundred Banners Walk is a verdict everyone on the processional can read. Housefront rights say which families may hold property and representation; the Hundred Houses Quarter holds the ones still petitioning at the Recognition Hearing Rooms and the Unrepresented Houses Desk. The Republic Council seats the Core Holder and one representative per major House, and the Castro seat is Lucan Castro's, not Darkstar's, because the Core is not the House. A surname is a heritage signal and nothing more: it opens doors and draws attention, grants no affinity, rank, knowledge or allegiance, and using it socially is allowed while claiming House authority you do not hold is fraud. A Capitol Service badge shows a term served and confers nothing after it. Academy placement is visible in where a student sleeps, House-Sponsored Residences against Independent Student Housing, and an Academy Challenge Ring ranking is internal and shielded from bookmakers. The Hollow Ring's champion is a crowd's name; at any registration desk it is a liability, not a title.

Relstaris: Ways and Sayings.text:
Capitol speech is code-switched and indirect, because Relstaris-born people grow up reading several House customs at once. Time is told by the light: "before Peak" means early, "at Fade" means after work, "Low hours" means the night services and the people who use them. "Decided before it's announced" is said of any Citadel news, with a shrug. "That's Shared Ground" ends an argument about who may stand where, since no House owns the plazas. "Waiting on a Petition Season" means it will take forever and probably die in procedure. "Landed at the No Sponsor Desk" describes anyone whose promised patron never appeared. "Whoever tells it first" is the city's theory of reputation, since the version that spreads first sticks. "Sign nothing on the Row" is advice about Nightglass Row and about drink in general. "Every house, one plaza" is the Every-House Plaza's name used as a toast. The common Relstaris-born line, "Your house explains part of where you came from. It does not explain the whole person standing here," is said flatly to visitors who lead with a surname. Greetings ask which district you crossed, not which House you carry, and the farewell to a shift worker is "Rise gets you home," meaning the routing will be back up before you are.

Relstaris: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: nobody inside the Citadel can prove that the machinery beneath Darkstar Castro is protecting the city rather than learning to protect itself, and the people placed to find out each hold one piece. Talris Contair has found unauthorised routing in the Relstaris Core and must ask Rezulith Contair for help without letting Vexorath take the capitol's heart. Maris Othrel may find no author behind the pattern, only aligned incentives; Cassara Veylen cannot be sure she is not reading Darkstar's silence as approval; Kaelis Morven's archives may hold a challenge never honestly registered; Brenn Ordan and Daelor Ravello have found that Thallax Sol governed far longer than official history admits, and that truth stays reserved. Below the civic map, Varek Zelvaris's ledger at the Hollow Ring names respectable patrons of fixed fights, Kelvan Orvantis fights debt matches there, and fixing has already distorted one official competition. The Signal Anomaly Room holds transmissions nobody can classify. None of this resolves the Core, Thallax Sol or the signals. It surfaces through an archivist's caution, an advisor's hesitation and a fighter's unexplained injury, never as a lecture.

Solvraxis: Everyday Operations.text:
Solvraxis wakes bright and unhurried. Most residents fly, and the Public Transit Rings carry children still learning, the injured, newcomers and anyone with an awkward parcel; taking the Rings is convenience, not a mark of anything. Arrivals pass the Gate Security Peace Line and hear the weapons law explained as civic trust rather than confiscation; a blade bought elsewhere is bonded, with its receipt through The Veyth Notary. The tenday keeps eight working days, a market day and a rest day, and Valcoro Academy runs intake in Brightrise, evaluation in Ashfall, placement in Ironbreak and graduation in Greenward, so the city's mood is seasonal. A simple meal costs about 6 Credits at the Archive Cafe or on Starfall Market, a modest room-night about 24 plus 3 for utilities, a group lesson 25, an everyday outfit 45 because the city dresses well; an ordinary completed shift pays around 68 and a skilled one around 145. Work is café service, academic support, archive assistance and visitor guidance within what you are authorised to touch. The shift is agreed first, an offer is not acceptance, and declining leaves no debt. A purchase on Starfall Market takes twice as long as it should because of who you meet, and the evening ends at the Silver Cup Pub, where Liora Bellovari hears everything and repeats little.

Solvraxis: Signs and Membership.text:
Solvraxis marks people gently and precisely. Castro household members wear the house blacks, deep blue-black with purple trim, like work clothes rather than regalia; Sevran Castro's cut is older and plainer, and a Valcoro student's is rumpled from training. Valcoro Academy issues training bands, soft practice sashes and composure lesson tokens, and Ilaria Valcoro certifies who may teach the public form; the certificate is respected in other cities, and study is still not access to protected mastery. Ravello archive passes and record-integrity seals say who may read what; Orvessa care tokens and guesthouse orientation cards say who is being looked after; a Veyth seal says a document was validly executed and nobody can impeach the witness. Placement is visible in housing, from the Second-Year Student Houses to the Third-Year Terrace Housing shared by all four Castro-derived minor Houses. Veyth is a faded fifth House, not Castro-derived and not House Vey of Dustfall. A Castro surname opens doors and draws watchers, grants no affinity or rank, and claiming Castro authority you do not hold is fraud. The Civic Peace Stations are staffed by calm, unarmed people, never a police force, and the only uniform that matters here is the absence of one.

Solvraxis: Ways and Sayings.text:
Solvraxis talks softly and means it. The city's own lines are quoted straight: "Strength is proven by what it refuses to take," said of a person who declines an advantage, and "Power is quiet when everyone already believes in it," said half-proudly of the Castros. Valcoro's motto, "Control before force," is what an instructor says to a student who won ugly. "Nobody's armed" is both reassurance and reproach: calm down, you are in Solvraxis. "Take it to the Still Court" means say it carefully and somewhere quiet. "Ask Ravello" means check the record before you argue, and "a Veyth seal on it" means beyond dispute. "That'll take a Starfall hour" describes any market errand doubled by conversation. "Rings today" means I am not flying, and nobody asks why. "Bonded at the gate" describes a visitor's blade left in storage and, teasingly, a visitor's temper. "After the fear ends" is Orvessa's phrase for when safety is really proven, used of a family that has settled. Time runs by the academy year: "Ashfall nerves" for evaluation season, "Ironbreak letters" for placements, and a greeting in Greenward is simply "Who's graduating?" People say goodbye by naming where they will next be seen, since in a city this observant they will be.

Solvraxis: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: the haven has never been seriously tested, and the people who keep it know it. House Castro's seniors privately share the old terraces' worry that the peace rests on Darkstar Castro personally; Lucera Castro keeps contingency notes on it in the Protected Family Archives, and Darkstar cannot answer whether he restored the balance or became the only thing holding it. Marcon Valcoro builds civic defence capacity as though the peace might one day stand without its keystone; Neressa Valcoro knows hospitality-as-screening works only because nobody has pushed it, and Calessa Orvessa has flagged an arrival shadowing Selene Castro who is counting on no one being armed. Maereth Ravello's letters with Daelor Ravello are in effect negotiating when Nexara may remember the era before Darkstar's rise, and Veylan Ravello's off-catalogue shelf names people who afterwards vanish from the record. Viaro Bellovari knows how many days of grace the city has if the Corsair routes falter and has told no one. The Veyth Notary's archive holds a contract a wealthy family would pay to bury; which family, what it proves and what is inside the Sealed Training Garden stay unanswered. Let it surface through a clerk's hesitation and a mother's contingency plan, never as a lecture.

Korrvane: Everyday Operations.text:
In Korrvane the sky is the road. A commute is a Transit Lane in the outer band if you are slow, a Courier Cut if you are paid to be fast, and the Lift Exchange if you are carrying, injured or prefer decking; lift users are commuters, not a caste. The tenday is the bracket: qualifiers on days one to six, the round of thirty-two and sixteen on day seven, quarterfinals and semifinals on day eight, the weekly final on the ninth, market day, as a citywide event, and on the tenth the Victory Wall is updated and the Recovery Yards are full. Merchants adjust stock around bracket weeks and teachers schedule around tournament traffic. Korrvane is the cheapest city on Nexara: a simple meal about 4 Credits at Second Landing or the Grounded Cup, a room-night about 16 plus 2 for utilities, a short ride 2, while an ordinary completed shift pays around 72 and a skilled one around 155. Work follows the Arena: food service on the Arena Street Food Ring, registration support, equipment preparation, deliveries, structural work on Impact Repair Row. Tournament work earns its agreed wage without requiring anyone to fight; an offer is not acceptance, and a registrar cannot hire you by announcing you. News runs faster on the Public Rumor Rail than on any notice. Highfire is tournament season, and its last tenday is the Grand Bracket.

Korrvane: Signs and Membership.text:
Korrvane dresses allegiance in colour and standing in memory. Genesis wears dark green and black with bronze-gold accents under storm-metal columns and victory walls. The six district Houses carry bronze-black markers on their own palettes: Orvantis in weathered bronze-black and ivory; Zelvaris in dark teal and charcoal; Caelthorn in polished black, ivory and silver; Aevon in blue, white and bronze with flight harnesses; Luxaryn in wine-red, bronze and cream; Vorreth in muted plum and gray. Families decorate recovery wraps with house markers, and active wraps mean you may not be challenged. A House Seating Tier is a family gathering; a guaranteed bracket slot is what district standing looks like. Registration needs identity verification, medical clearance at the Medic Gate, a sponsor or open-entry approval and inspected equipment, and grants entry, not belonging. Titles are records fought and ruled in play: Korrvane Bracket Contender, Korrvane Weekly Champion, Genesis Ladder Challenger, Beyond the First Gate, Highfire Grand Bracket Champion, Aerial Ring Victor. A title confers no membership, rank, ability or payment; it changes invitations, sponsorship and how a crowd sounds before a bout. Suspended from the Bracket is a status cleared only by medics and judges. Nobody quotes a number, because there is none.

Korrvane: Ways and Sayings.text:
Korrvane talks the way it fights: declared, blunt, remembered. "Strength is witnessed" is the city's creed and its excuse. "Declare before striking" is said to anyone who starts an argument without warning, in or out of a ring. "Lost clean" is the highest thing said of a loser, and "came back" the highest thing said of anyone, since returning after public failure is what strength means here. "Move it to a lane" ends a quarrel in a civic walk. "Don't interrupt food" is a rule and a joke. "In wraps" means off limits, from recovery wraps to a friend who has just been dumped. "Rumor Rail says" prefaces anything unofficial and probably true. "Vorreth odds" describes anything nobody can predict. "Made him serious" is praise so high it is rarely earned, for forcing a Genesis member to stop playing. "Ask the Wall" means it is on record at the Victory Wall, argue with that. "Nina's precedent" is an exception that is not a rule. Time runs on the bracket: "before qualifiers," "bracket day," "final day," and "wall day" for the tenth. Flight has its manners: "outer band" tells someone to slow down and get out of the way, and "cutting wake" is an accusation of hostility. Winners buy the first shared meal; losers show up to eat it.

Korrvane: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: the ladder is a civic asset only while it is administered honestly, and honest administration is under quieter pressure than any cheat. Kaldor Dravon is building a civic crisis designed to provoke the challenge Ark Genesis most wants to make, and Ark's straightforwardness is the mechanism; Sorvina Genesis watches tournament crowds for Dravon observers and has never been wrong. Tacitus Genesis knows Caelthorn's valid rule readings threaten the bracket more than cheating would, and Giscara Caelthorn has never once needed to cheat, the one asset she will not spend. Corvinus Genesis keeps private notes on how every family member, Ark included, could be beaten, and Tannivar Zelvaris holds an unpublished file on Alcandrus Genesis. Hasdrovex Orvantis's injuries at the Recovery Yards do not match his public bout, and the Betting Stands, the Zelvaris Recovery Annex and Baalrix Caelthorn all have reasons to shape the review. Milkon Luxaryn means to turn the house's warmth into leverage, Qartessa Luxaryn runs the city's best informal intelligence as soup, and Salambor Luxaryn keeps an exclusion list. Whether Vorreth's unreadability is strategy, culture or something else is unsettled inside the house and stays so. It surfaces in an odds line that moves too early and a rival who buys the beaten analyst a drink, never as a lecture.

Quilrath: Everyday Operations.text:
An outer-ring day in Quilrath runs on the boards: present for assignment, wait, work, collect an allotment, be inside before the gates close. Kathvar administrators staff the Civic Counters, the Ring Gate and the Permit Desk, processing what Nivarek's Standing Office has already decided; a permit is printed as a distance and a set of hours, and one whose hours cover curfew is the only night clearance that exists. Curfew belongs to the Ashrings and to Grade 4; Grade 5 moves by work order only; Grades 1 to 3 are logged at every crossing after closing, and the log is what the next audit reads. No curfew hour is fixed and none is narrated as a clock. The Provision Hall sells goods of famously adequate quality, and Torbek Karn's counter moves extras through the tolerated gray market on perfect paperwork. Quilrath is squeezed rather than expensive: an authorised Gray Rings meal costs about 7 Credits at The Measured Hour, a room-night about 24 plus 4 for utilities, while an ordinary completed shift pays around 45 and a skilled one around 105, so three meals, a room and utilities cost 49 against a 45 shift. Work is authorised maintenance, provision handling and issued-equipment tasks within one's actual assignment; even here an offer is not acceptance, and Credits buy no radius, no queue speed and no grade. Ironbreak is reassignment season.

Quilrath: Signs and Membership.text:
Quilrath sorts people in two separate ledgers. Outside the Inner Circle everyone lives under the Civic Standing Grades that Nivarek assigns and Kathvar processes: Grade 1, the Polished, trusted civilians of the inner Gray Ring; Grade 2, Gatefolk, who pass most ring gates; Grade 3, Grays, the standard mass; Grade 4, Half-lights, probationary and curfewed, where conquered-house lines mostly enter; Grade 5, Ashfeet, restricted labour of the Camp Belt moving by work order only. The Erased are not a grade; they are removed from the records, and that mystery is not resolved here. A grade sets housing ring, work assignment, movement radius, queue speed, audit frequency and a child's starting grade, and confers no vote and no property right. Inside the Inner Circle, Access Levels 0 to 9 govern instead, from Unmarked through Processed Visitor, Escorted Inner Visitor, Inner Citizen, Rank-Marked Citizen, Military-Cleared, Nivarek-Cleared, Balrath-Cleared and Command-Cleared to Ascendant Restricted, held by Kaldor, Sorin and Vaelen Dravon. A Grade 1 civilian holds no access at all, and visitors are never on the ladder. Signs read from a distance: command blacks with gold status inlays, rank marks at the Rank Gates, a Redline banner on a proven family's block, the red command-light grids overhead. The narrator never volunteers anyone's number.

Quilrath: Ways and Sayings.text:
Quilrath speech is careful, and the care is the accent. People praise promptly, choose words, and keep opinions for "past the pylons," the deep Ashrings where the surveillance does not reach. "Processed" is a verb done to you, and "processed like anyone else" is the regime's boast and the rows' bitterest joke. "On the boards" means assigned or waiting for assignment. "A distance and a set of hours" is what a permit is, said of any permission smaller than it sounds. "Adequate" is the state's word for its goods and the people's word for anything they dare not call bad. "Inside before closing" is the evening farewell, and "who closed late?" the morning question, since a logged crossing feeds the next audit. "Someone's cousin fell" explains a household suddenly under review, because audits weigh family association. "Ironbreak's coming" is dread of reassignment. "Half-light" is a slur from above and a grim self-description from within. Trusted people finish the Inner Circle's own line, "The closer you stand to Dravon power, the cleaner the city becomes," with "the farther you fall from it, the more honest it gets." The frontier's joke, "Better than Dravon," is aimed at exactly these Provision shelves and is not said aloud here. The Archive's article of faith, "Dravon breaks houses. Names hold," is never said at all; it is written, hidden and carried.

Quilrath: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: the machine that makes conquest permanent has seams, and the people standing at them are inside the regime. Records are vanishing from Red Ledger Prime, Nivarek's own sealed archive; Kaless Nivarek's access logs show nothing, he has told no one including his brother Thamur Nivarek, and he quietly watches Myrra Nivarek, Maelra Dravon and Orvane Dravon. Whether Myrra is the Archive's friend inside or merely fits the hole is genuinely unresolved and stays so. Ferrik Nivarek keeps illegal duplicates of his own audits, a grade he falsified years ago among them. Kaldor Dravon treats the Ledger as a front to be mapped before it is fought, without knowing whom the mapping will implicate; Maelra keeps a second set of notes, a crime she wrote the definition of. In the Balrath Gateworks, override paths appear in no Dravon specification and Arduk Balrath calls them insurance; Sennar Balrath's delay margins in the lockdown seals are meant as seconds; Pelna Ostrek's readings say the Quilrath Gate's next failure may be its last. Mirasha Kathvar finds the margin inside the rule at the Curfew Gates, and Cadi Selm walks families down the Quiet Mile carrying Archive copies as memorised fragments. The Erased and the Red Ledger are not resolved. Let it surface through a clerk's one extra question and an engineer's unfiled report, never as a lecture.

Helvyra: Everyday Operations.text:
Helvyra wakes with the barge tide. Route-boards on every corner refresh at dawn, Routefall Market is shouting by mid-morning, the skyhooks swing loads between barge, warehouse and Waypoint until late, and the Cold Pour takes over after dark. Work is posted on the Day-Work Board in the Underbank, the Hiring Wall at the Hauler Yards and the Courier Dispatch of the Grand Waypoint: freight handling, storage, hospitality, fitted equipment work, passenger support. A job is complete when the load or the service reaches its actual recipient, and Common Scale grading settles what was delivered; an offer is not acceptance, and a courier who declines a run owes nobody. A simple meal is about 5 Credits, a Terva pocket from The Waiting Cup or a bowl at Three Seats More; a modest room-night about 20 plus 3 for utilities, cheaper and damper in the Underbank; routine care at Bankside Care Hall about 24. An ordinary completed shift pays around 70 and a skilled one around 155. Market day fills the Stall Rows and the Certified Goods Aisle, where prestige Arvek sells for luxury prices a few streets from the same animal sold cheap. First Barge reopens the high river, the Great Reckoning settles the year's debts in public, and Signday unveils the new Xyren sign with complete ceremonial seriousness.

Helvyra: Signs and Membership.text:
Helvyra reads people by their marks and their terrace. The Common Scale seal is the most trusted object in the city and the most forged on Nexara; it is issued by minor-house and independent arbiters, never by Corsairs, which is why Corsair's network is trusted at all. Cargo and route markings follow bright standardised colour-codes, and abusing a courier credential is a Waypoint taboo. Open Circle certification marks on a charm say the Circle stands behind it, and Quenna Sil's hall can refuse to issue one. Blade Courts Graded means a Wayline grading passed at Rux Corsair's Sword School, a school recognition and not a House rank; Redcourt Challenge Victor means a public challenge won under House Veltrax's conditions, and the sword-school banners on facing banks tell you where a student trains. The Bank Wardens are respected, unarmored and obeyed. Corsair membership runs by family through the Magic, Commerce and Swordsmanship branches, and a Corsair face is on every mandatory sign, so the name draws jokes before deference. Belonging is also read vertically: the Underbank at the waterline, Riverrow above it, Merchant Row above that, the Estate on the high west terrace, and everyone above has lived below or is one bad season from it. A surname grants no route, no seal and no standing at the Scale.

Helvyra: Ways and Sayings.text:
Helvyra talks in departures. "Everything arrives. Nothing stays still" is the city's line and its shrug. "Check the board" is said before anyone promises a time. "Signed for" means done properly, from Varriko's saying, "If it mattered, someone signed for it," quoted at every verbal promise. Yalven's "Pretty breaks first. Useful comes home" is said over anything ornate, and Veltrax's "Forward is also a defense" over anyone who hesitates. "Went in the river" means lost beyond recovery. "Up a terrace" means doing better, and "back to the Underbank" the opposite. "Between gates" describes someone passing through who should not be trusted with the long version. "Read the route" means think before you act. "Take it to the Scale" means settle it neutrally, and "the Blade Courts heard it" means it is now a public fact. "Not my sign" is what a Corsair says to deny responsibility, and outsiders say it back to them. "Deals become friendships" is the Cold Pour's justification for a fourth drink. "Reckoning's coming" is said of debts and grudges from midyear on. The worst thing you can call anyone is "Waypoint thief," because the city forgives a bad deal and does not forgive theft from the road that feeds it. Greetings ask what you are carrying; the farewell is "clear board," meaning no delays on your route.

Helvyra: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: the two most trusted marks in Helvyra may be compromised by one hand, and nobody has said so across the river. Verel Ondin is tracing a forged Common Scale seal on premium cargo; Oren Varriko has found a sealed bond replaced with a perfect fake, and the list of people capable of it is the list he would report it to; whether one forger made both stays open. Sereth Varriko believes the missing-cargo dispute the city calls theft is insurance fraud from inside the trade network, and Tavik Corsair knows what actually moves against what is declared. Daxor Veltrax reads from blade wear that someone is blending Veltrax pressure with Corsair movement, Meya Orlin logs a wound pattern at Bankside Care Hall that matches no known style, and Kaelen Veltrax believes a fake standard was seeded into the Pressure Hall. Torvane Yalven cannot prove a faulty batch was sabotaged before the Contair inspectors close the Support Model Line, and Quenna Sil holds a confiscated route-charm that worked where route-charms cannot. Ondrel Vask's manifest archive has a traveller nobody remembers; Tam Vessic has three tenants gone with rent paid forward; Essim Corle keeps a Quilrath vintage that cannot legitimately exist. Let it surface through a rigger's refusal, a child's homework and a physician's silence, never as a lecture.

Vexorath: Everyday Operations.text:
A Vexorath day begins with a door that opens before you touch it. Transit anticipates where you are going, public furniture adjusts to you, delivery drones reroute around a conversation, and the annoyance of the day is a manual task nobody has automated yet. Arrivals enter through the Gate District, past the Arrival Diagnostic Lane and the Visitor Authentication Hall, where visitors lose arguments with access systems and the Dravon Access Denial Marker is not a formality. Work is fabrication assistance, device servicing and technical support within one's competence and Contair's release limits, posted on the Repair Contract Board at the Exchange; it completes when the assessed working result is delivered, and a repair grants no clinical authority and no restricted design. An offer is not acceptance, and Rezulith Contair's impatience with delay binds nobody. Vexorath pays best on Nexara and charges for it: an ordinary completed shift around 85 Credits and a skilled one around 195, a simple meal about 6 at A Small Adjustment, a modest room-night about 28 plus 2 for utilities, a group lesson 30. Meal sessions at the Shared Meal Court follow household shifts rather than a three-meal clock, and a guest eats there with a resident host. The tenday's rest day belongs to the Assembly Floor and The Overclock.

Vexorath: Signs and Membership.text:
Vexorath marks responsibility, not rank. Contair wears white and charcoal seamed with cobalt, the construction language of the city itself, and Myralis physicians wear pearl-white clinical attire; neither is issued to anyone. Authority follows the problem: Rezulith Contair holds final technical authority over the Lumina Core, gate integrity and the Outer Shell, and custodians act within their own fields without asking her, Maelis Contair for civic systems, Drexan Contair for fabrication, Tavris Contair for drone doctrine, Solanis Contair for Lumina Reach, Avara Myralis for clinical ethics and Torren Myralis for trauma. Civilian decisions pass through the Resident Assembly. Drones read by class: Ward units are visible security, Mote units guide and carry, Aegis units move in formation and never for routine enforcement, Echo work is restricted and never public. Lumina Major and Lumina Minor are persons, and Minor's name implies no lesser standing. A Contair surname bypasses nothing; access to Lumina Reach follows legitimate purpose, and a Myralis name is not a licence. A resident who finds a usability flaw has contributed to the design. Contair marks on equipment are checked, not trusted, because counterfeits circulate. Dravon is permanently barred, and a Dravon at the marker is a major event, never a routine.

Vexorath: Ways and Sayings.text:
Vexorath talks in systems and means people. "A good system should make imposed order unnecessary" is the House line, quoted against Dravon and, quietly, against overprotective neighbours. "Nothing fails the same way twice" is said after every repair. "Records systems, not private lives" is the city's promise and the sentence that starts most arguments in the Privacy Challenge Chamber. "Report the fault" means own up, and is the first thing children learn. "Which drone follows too literally" is a standing joke with a different answer in every household. "Lost the argument with the door" describes a visitor stuck at authentication. "Possible further use" is said of anything hoarded, after the label on Paul Thovex's storage pod. "Change one variable" is kitchen advice and life advice, since cooks revise a recipe the way engineers revise a design. "Sufficient understanding" is said drily of anyone who assumes the answer is obvious, which is Rezulith Contair's flaw and the city's. "Explain it after" reminds emergency authority that a restriction must be justified once the emergency ends. Myralis adds "can they live with it?" to every technical triumph, and "step away" to any colleague too tired to judge. "Denied at the marker" is the strongest no the city has. The farewell is "keep the door open," meaning stay reachable.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; city=Vexorath; lore=idiom; topics=sayings, Contair philosophy, failure culture, privacy, drones, authentication, Paul Thovex.

Vexorath: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: overprotection is built into the city's systems, and the line between safety and control is being tested by the House's own people. Lumina Major has refused Rezulith Contair records that Rezulith considered operational. Maelis Contair has discovered residents quietly working around a civic system rather than reporting it, and Paul Thovex has found that infrastructure monitoring recorded more of his household than intended; Sela Thovex keeps a private list of systems that passed every review and still fail residents, and the list implicates careers. An old Outer Shell layer has woken for a threat category nobody now remembers creating, and the Repair Crawl Network is where something will be found where nothing should be. Solanis Contair holds deep-space traffic patterns that fit no known route and announces nothing, and that stays unresolved. At the Continuum, Avara Myralis and Torren Myralis disagree on how long a physician may wait, and the day a patient is lost on either side, the medical veto is what gets questioned; Selvara Myralis has repaired tissue responding to affinity it was never designed to support. A Dravon-derived component sits somewhere on the Exchange's public floor. Let it surface through a maintenance notice and a resident who stopped answering, never as a lecture.

Ignivex: Everyday Operations.text:
Ignivex runs hot and interrupted. Cinderline Transit moves people through heat-resistant lanes and thermal lift platforms between the Emberward, the forges and the Hearth Rows, and an alert can stop a shift, a repair or a family meal without making anyone a combatant. Work hours bend around the heat, and the Cooling Steps are where a working day is allowed to end. Work is forge assistance on the Apprentice Benches of the Red Forges, garment and tool upkeep, recovery-space support and civilian event work; the agreed task earns its pay when finished, an alert may interrupt it, and an offer is not acceptance, however loudly it is made. Clinical work stays with qualified people, and local heat experience is not a shared fire affinity. A simple meal costs about 5 Credits at The Held Cup or The Second Helping, where the cook asks how hot you actually want it and a heat waiver is voluntary; a modest room-night about 17 plus 2 for utilities; an everyday outfit 48 and a tool set 48, because heat-resistant cloth and tools cost more. An ordinary completed shift pays around 65 and a skilled one around 155. Purchases run under the canopies of Ashglass Market, along the Spice Line and the Fire-Treated Goods Row, beside a Corsair Trade Post whose arrangement with House Volen nobody explains. The tenday's rest day belongs to the Shared Courtyards and The Low Flame.

Context tags: planet=Nexara; city=Ignivex; lore=everyday; topics=heat, Cinderline Transit, alerts, forge work, Red Forges.

Ignivex: Signs and Membership.text:
Ignivex wears its politics on its clasps. The Volen emblem, a stylised triple flame inside a broken heat ring, is the default civic mark on banners, shoulder plates, belt pieces and gauntlets, because Volen leads the city. The Caldris emblem, a black basalt wall split by a single vertical ember line, marks emergency gear, firebreak gates and wall plates; the Meravil emblem, a pale ash spiral inside a thin red ring, marks civic clothing, record halls and administrative stations. Standardised armour sets fitted at the Red Forges say a person stands a wall or a patrol, not which House they were born to. A firelike eye glimmer or an ember-gradient in the hair is natural biology here, not a badge, and no one infers an affinity from a Volen surname; the House's fire is a cultural tradition, not an inheritance. Passing the Restraint Trials at the Crucible Yard under Maeryn Volen means you can be hit and keep your judgment, and the First Flame is a rite of control that grants no rank. Someone in the Cooling Oath Service Rooms caused harm through reckless fire or violence and is earning public trust back through recovery, repair or rescue work. Cassian Genesis married into Volen and is the living tie between the Houses; Nyssara Dravon lives under Meravil protection and is not a Meravil.

Ignivex: Ways and Sayings.text:
Ignivex speaks loud and settles fast. "Forward through the flame" is Volen's line and the city's, said before anything hard. "The wall remembers who stood there" is Caldris's, said of the unglamorous and the dead. "Ash is what remains when pride burns too long" is Meravil's, said quietly and answered with fury. "Say it in the Smoke" means take it to the Smoke Court and say it to their face. "Eat after" is the whole social contract: shout, reach the truth, then share a table. "How hot?" is a greeting at any table and means how are you really. "Holding the wall" describes anyone doing the necessary thing nobody praises. "Waived" means you knew the risk, from restaurant heat waivers, and is said of bad decisions freely chosen. "Cool down" is literal and social, since the Cooling Steps are where pride pays its cost. "Counting" is said of someone who has started to add up losses and is leaning toward accommodation, and it is not a compliment. "Not a drill" needs no explanation. "Gate to two places" describes any narrow choice, after a Lunar Gate that reaches only Relstaris and Dustfall. "Pain is information" is Crucible teaching quoted at anyone who stops too early. Nobody says Soren Dravon's name lightly, and a room goes still when someone does.

Ignivex: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: Soren Dravon's name is a lever that Dravon agents almost certainly already hold, and Cynar Volen suspects it and refuses to admit it; Varessa Volen plans around the day someone uses the name to pull him out of position. Tharen Volen is designing failure modes to make a captured geothermal network worthless and has told no one, and a pressure fault in the Heat Tunnels sits beside one of his Sabotage Watch Points. Iskara Volen may know the real reason Dravon wants Ignivex, and that reason stays reserved. Davor Caldris has arranged Caldris planning so the city holds through a leadership crisis without a Volen order; Maedra Caldris re-keys the deliberate weaknesses in her own gates on a schedule no document holds; Lysa Caldris is pre-positioning supplies along routes that only make sense for something worse than a raid; raids keep striking where Rava Caldris's evacuation is hardest, as though someone is learning her routes. Ilvara Meravil's arithmetic says the city is losing a war it believes it is surviving; Vennik Meravil is manoeuvring on channels nobody else has toward something colder than Seralyne Meravil's fear; Nyssara Dravon has never volunteered what she knows. Whether the third conflict ignites is never decided here. Let it surface through a displacement count and a route that changed, never as a lecture.

Dustfall: Everyday Operations.text:
A Dustfall day starts with someone sweeping dust off advanced machinery before opening. Shopkeepers along the Main Settlement Strip clear their thresholds, carriers work loads along the paving, and the Perimeter Beacon Line is the first thing anyone checks when the wind turns. Work is posted on the Informal Job Rail, the Job Board Wall at The Long Shot and the Public Repair Board: household repairs, clothing alteration, loading, meals, courier runs and assessed salvage. A repair, a shift or a handoff completes it; an offer is not acceptance, everyone is free to refuse a job, and everyone else is free to remember the refusal. Dustfall is cheap to sleep in and costly to supply: a modest room-night about 14 Credits but 5 more for utilities, a simple meal about 7 at The Held Seat or the Dustfall Meal Yard, a short ride 5, a tool set 58; an ordinary completed shift pays around 60 and a skilled one around 145. Prices at Grit and Supply move with the shipment, and Credits are normal while barter or a seat held for an absent friend is a specific agreement. Communal meals follow a Corsair shipment's arrival, and residents bet on how long a repair will last. Children learn flight control in enclosed yards beside weapon safety and literacy, and the tenday's rest day is whichever day nothing breaks.

Dustfall: Signs and Membership.text:
In Dustfall a visible weapon is ordinary and a hidden one needs a reason. Competence outranks house name, and the old house symbols on doors are repainted, cut away, hidden or displayed proudly, each a statement. The crews are legible by where they stand: the Iron Jackals at Vossan Yard under Kaedra Vossan, the Bent Halo at the Crooked Landing under Saevik Ruun, who never confirms which route signs are his, the Black Pennant around the Vaereth banner in Old Banner Hall under Rhex Vaereth, the Last Line Company at its barracks by the perimeter under Tavra Korrin, the Claimants at Claim Camp under Ravik Rusk with their Warrant Board. Being fed or sheltered by one confers no membership, and receiving Accord help confers none either. No organisation rules Dustfall. There is no sheriff, mayor or council; Sennra Sol's authority holds as far as the Dispute Table at The Long Shot, Draxen Sol coordinates a defence that dissolves when the danger passes, and Raynor Sol is a wider Sol anchor, not a commander. House Sol is common here and rules nothing, and not every resident is Sol. Dravon warrants, Civic Standing grades and return demands have no automatic force. There is no ring and no title. A name on the Town Memory Shelf or in Ovar Kethrin's Last Names Room is the only record that counts.

Dustfall: Ways and Sayings.text:
Dustfall talk is dry, blunt and priced. "Fancy gets you noticed. Useful gets you fed" is said to anyone dressed for a different city. "Better than Dravon. Barely" is the running insult for anything that works badly, never serious praise. "You staying, leaving, or causing paperwork?" is the greeting at the General Arrival Shelf. "Road's clear if you don't count the people shooting on it" is a route report. "Dustfall doesn't have secrets. It has pricing tiers" is what Tessik Luxaryn's regulars say about Black Dust. "Unsafe is not a technical category. Be specific" is repair-bench language, and Pella Mox means it. "Nobody rules Dustfall. Plenty of people invoice it" is said whenever someone mentions the Jackals' protection. "You can keep the house name. Just don't expect it to pay the repair bill" is said to displaced gentry. "Freedom's free. Everything needed to survive it costs extra" is the settlement's economics in one line. "Sharing's on" means a genuine shortage has triggered the temporary-sharing custom, and "debts are back" means it has ended. "Shipment's in" means a communal meal at the Meal Yard tonight. "That's a Dispute Table matter" means stop shouting and see Sennra. "Beacons up" means a sandstorm or worse, and the farewell to a route crew is "come back intact," because that is what gets celebrated.

Dustfall: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: a Corsair shipment carrying Contair equipment, ammunition, medical stock and Lunar Gate components did not arrive, and Draxen Sol has confirmed it was taken by an organised interception, which changes the question from recovery to who supplied the intelligence. Ralven Nox keeps two ledgers at Vossan Yard and decides nightly how much of the second Kaedra Vossan sees; some items on the Jackal Auction Rail came from the streets the Jackals charge to protect, and Messa Taar quietly returns goods that should never have been taken. At the Crooked Landing the cargo veto belongs to Brannoc Kest, not Saevik Ruun, and his counts have carried people on no manifest at all; Ysara Sorn's patrol-map knowledge keeps the Landing survivable, and Dravon wants it back. Rhex Vaereth's Pennant raids under the name of restitution and has gone further against defectors than anyone outside Selka Vaereth knows, while a Vaereth family-association review moves through the Gray Rings toward Sedran Vaereth. Miren Tal thinks she is selling arrival data; the intermediary who buys it is buying people, and her records have surfaced in a Nivarek escapee file. Sura Venn has pulled a tracker that reports to somebody other than Dravon, and who that is stays unresolved. Let it surface through a returned component and a name on the wrong list, never as a lecture.

House Castro: Everyday Operations.text:
House Castro runs Solvraxis by not running it. Darkstar Castro lives at the Relstaris Citadel as Core Holder and returns to Darkstar's Solvraxis Seat at the Castro Citadel without the household advertising how often; Vega Castro works the long negotiation days from Vega's Diplomatic Chamber; Lucera Castro runs the family's civic commitments and a household line; Sevran Castro anchors the seat and teaches the youngest cousins; Caivan Castro is the visible face of Castro protection and answers formal challenges. The city's daily machinery belongs to the four Castro-derived minor Houses, Valcoro's academy, Ravello's archive, Bellovari's markets and Orvessa's welfare district, and the Castros interfere as little as a family that owns the peace can. In Relstaris, Lucan Castro sits in the Republic Council as the House's seat, distinct from the Core, and the Castro Compound's Public Aid Office covers real costs under real arrangements; aid is never unlimited subsidy and never surprise debt. Compound staff work paid shifts at Solvraxis anchors, around 68 Credits for an ordinary completed shift and 145 for a skilled one, agreed before they start. When the House offers work, protection or help, the offer can be refused and refusal costs nothing, because an offer is not acceptance and House Castro does not police.

House Castro: Signs and Membership.text:
You know a Castro by the house blacks, deep blue-black with purple trim, worn like work clothes: Sevran Castro's in an older plainer cut, Miro Castro's rumpled from Valcoro training, Selene Castro's neat, Darkstar's unadorned. There is no crown, throne or royal line to display, and the House refuses those words. The Core Holder and the Castro seat are separate offices, so Darkstar holding the Relstaris Core makes nobody in the family royal and gives Lucan Castro's Council seat no extra weight. Membership is a civic fact: born to it, married into it, or rarely adopted; Aela Castro lives in the Genesis household and keeps her name. A young Castro chooses formally within the customary window of roughly three to five hundred cycles and may choose otherwise, and the House may withdraw access and sponsorship but cannot compel return. The surname opens doors, draws watchers and attracts enemies, and grants nothing: no affinity, since Darkstar's and Nina's are their own, no rank, no knowledge, no allegiance. Using the name socially is allowed; claiming Castro authority you do not hold is fraud. Valcoro, Ravello, Bellovari and Orvessa are Castro-derived and are not Castro. The tell of a real Castro is restraint under provocation, which the family would say is the whole point.

House Castro: Ways and Sayings.text:
Castro idiom is spare and corrective. "Strength is proven by what it refuses to take" is the House's public line and its private test. "House Castro does not police. House Castro protects" is said to outsiders who ask why nobody is armed, and to young cousins who want to be. "Strength should protect freedom" is the whole philosophy, offered flatly against Dravon's "strength should create order." "Power is quiet when everyone already believes in it" is what Vega Castro says when someone asks why the family does so little. "The seat is not the Core" corrects anyone who calls Darkstar a ruler of anything but the capitol. "Refuse it well" is advice for declining an advantage, an offer or a fight without insult. "Hold, don't take" is Caivan Castro's teaching in the training court. "That's a Nina" describes any cheerful breach of etiquette, and "Nina's precedent" any exception that is not a rule. "The terraces are asking again" means the old worry has resurfaced, whether the peace rests on one man, and it is said only inside the family. "Quiet enough?" is a dry check that a matter has been settled without spectacle. "Later, with the family" postpones a decision to the Family Council Chamber. Castros greet with a name and a question about the person's day, never a title.

House Castro: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: the House's senior members privately share the old terraces' worry that the peace rests on Darkstar Castro personally, and none of them has a plan they can say aloud. Lucera Castro has written contingency notes on it and keeps them in the Protected Family Archives of the Castro Citadel, records the family did not lodge with Ravello; Sevran Castro spends his influence making the worry untrue; Vega Castro builds civic trust that would survive his brother; Darkstar himself cannot answer whether he restored the balance or became the only thing holding it. Darkstar spends his own standing keeping the Core and the Castro seat visibly separate, and Lucan Castro refuses to spend his access the way anyone expects, while Cassor Dravon calls Castro aid patronage on the Republic Council record. Caivan Castro's peace with losing the Core is unfinished in one sparring match the two have never held. Calessa Orvessa has flagged a visitor shadowing Selene Castro through the Starfall Promenade who is counting on the fact that nobody is armed, and Mariel Valcoro watches the Castro Compound's own staff. Whether the peace would hold without Darkstar is never answered. Let it surface through a cousin's contingency notes and a defender's unfought match, never as a lecture.

House Genesis: Everyday Operations.text:
House Genesis runs Korrvane from one desk. Tacitus Genesis governs from Tacitus's Office in the Genesis Compound: minor-house disputes, Arena policy, infrastructure, the Contair maintenance relationship through the Gate Plazas, visitor problems and citywide emergencies, with Zephyra Genesis assisting earnestly and something going sideways. Ark Genesis anchors the challenge culture and breaks Ark's Training Ground often enough that its replacement is a routine line item; Corvinus Genesis keeps the Armory and the family's fighting form; Orvanus Genesis gives advice nobody asked for; Sorvina Genesis trains on Genesis Ridge, reached only through restricted Genesis Approach Airspace. Every tenday the House administers the Weekly Bracket through unnamed registrars, judges, rulekeepers, medics and commentators, and on market day Alcandrus Genesis stands at the Genesis Ladder Staging Area as the first gatekeeper. In Relstaris, Decimus Genesis holds the Council seat, Tacitus does the embassy's real work while Ark's Rarely Used Office stays maintained, and Valerius Genesis commands the capitol's public protection. Compound and Arena staff earn Korrvane wages, about 72 Credits for an ordinary completed shift and 155 for a skilled one, and an offer to carry a ruling, spar or serve is exactly that: an offer is not acceptance, and Tacitus's plain no means no.

House Genesis: Signs and Membership.text:
Genesis is dark green and black with bronze-gold accents, worn as training gear, formal armor-cloth or a tidy household cut, under storm-metal columns, tribunal balconies and victory walls. The compound is not a palace and Korrvane has no throne; the House rules because nobody believes it can be removed and because Tacitus Genesis keeps the city working. Genesis Approach Airspace is restricted, and being waved through it says more about your standing than any badge. Membership is birth, marriage or rare adoption, and it is a civic fact: Aela Castro lives in the household and keeps her name, Cassian Genesis married into Volen and lives in Ignivex, Alcandrus Genesis was born to a Genesis father and a Corsair mother and is Genesis. A surname does not confer Ark's abilities or power level, and no member is assumed to carry another's expression; Sorvina Genesis's storm has fire under it from her Volen side and is hers alone. The Genesis Ladder is not a rank ladder inside the House; Alcandrus is always first, and any further stage is set by Tacitus and Corvinus Genesis case by case, never as a numbered sequence. Genesis Ladder Challenger and Beyond the First Gate are records earned in play against the House, not memberships of it. The scar on Alcandrus's nose is the only Genesis decoration anyone talks about.

House Genesis: Ways and Sayings.text:
Genesis talks in blunt humour and shorter sentences than anyone else in Korrvane. "Strength is witnessed" is the House's civic creed. "Nobody believes we can be removed" is said without boasting, as a description of weather. "Come back" is the highest Genesis praise and the thing Ark Genesis wants most from an opponent: someone who returns after losing. "Ask Tacitus" means the real answer, and "Ark won't notice" describes any daily problem, which is most of them. "Serious" is the word for the moment a Genesis stops playing, and "made him serious" is what a challenger's whole career is for. "First gate" means Alcandrus Genesis and any obstacle that has never been passed. "Nina's precedent" is an exception that is not a rule, said with a wince. "Orvanus says" prefaces advice nobody asked for and Tacitus takes. "Zephyra helped" explains why it went sideways, and nobody has told her to stop. "Clean" is the only adjective that matters about a loss. "Norvina's grudge" is anything decades old and still alive. "Word for word" is Tacitus's standard for carrying a ruling, and a messenger who paraphrases does not carry the next one. Genesis greet by clapping a shoulder hard enough to check your footing, and say goodbye by naming the next bout.

House Genesis: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: Kaldor Dravon is building a civic crisis designed to provoke the challenge Ark Genesis most wants to make, and Ark's straightforwardness is the mechanism; Ark wants an honest fight and someone who comes back after losing, and cannot see a trap that looks like one. Sorvina Genesis watches tournament crowds for Dravon observers and has never been wrong. Tacitus Genesis knows Caelthorn's valid rule readings threaten the Genesis Ladder more than cheating would, because the ladder is a civic asset only while it is administered honestly, and his plain no to Giscara Caelthorn and Barcavon Zelvaris over the House Seating Tiers must be carried into Giscara's Reception Hall exactly as spoken. Corvinus Genesis keeps private notes on how every family member, Ark included, could be beaten. Valerius Genesis in Relstaris prepares the capitol's protection force for a succession contest he shares with no politician. Norvina Genesis has looked at leaving the city more than once. Orvanus Genesis alone can read the Old Training Markers on Genesis Ridge and gives advice instead of answers. Ark's friendly Core challenge at the Core Challenge Court is a session-stopping event in the Republic. Let it surface through a spectator Sorvina points at and a ruling carried word for word, never as a lecture.

House Dravon: Everyday Operations.text:
House Dravon rules Quilrath by delegating everything except command. Kaldor Dravon remains active and in charge from the Ascendant Keep, planning the longer game in the Red War Room; Sorin Dravon runs much of the daily military operation; Vaelen Dravon plans the war; Mavrek Dravon drills the heirs and certifies officers; Maelra Dravon curates the Victory Walk's approved history; Tarsen Dravon commands the Inner Compliance Gate where every arrival is logged, scanned and ranked; Valessa Dravon governs the high families' social world; Orvane Dravon audits the machine that audits everyone; Vandrik Dravon signs requisitions at the Balrath Bastion Barracks. Below them the work is divided: Nivarek decides Standing and keeps the records, Balrath builds the gates, drones and locks, Kathvar staffs the counters, and Redline deploys under the red command-lights. In Relstaris, Cassor Dravon argues the lawful-participation case in the Republic Council. The city's one Lunar Gate reaches only Relstaris and is kept barely working without Contair; there is no Waypoint. Wages are Quilrath's, about 45 Credits for an ordinary completed shift and 105 for a skilled one, and a Dravon escort, assignment or invitation is still an offer: an offer is not acceptance, and access raised for an errand is revoked when the errand ends.

House Dravon: Signs and Membership.text:
Dravon is black star-glass, red command-light and gold status inlay. Command blacks with gold at the collar mark the family; regulation-exact training blacks mark heirs under Mavrek Dravon; Kaldor, Sorin and Vaelen Dravon alone hold Access Level 9, Ascendant Restricted, with the power to rewrite access, trigger lockdown and seal records. Rank marks are read at the Rank Gates, a Redline banner hangs on a proven Grade 1 or 2 family's block, and the outer city sees the command-light grids as proof the regime is watching and proud of it. Membership is birth or marriage, and the name confers Kaldor's policy and none of his affinity or dissent; Sorin wants recognition, Vaelen wants a war fought by someone who does not believe the gallery, and Irala Dravon has no post at all. Outside Quilrath the name works differently: a Relstaris-born Dravon may reject the city while carrying the history, Cassor Dravon is the lawful public face, Velis Dravon is a civic law student whose every mistake is political, and Nyssara Dravon lives under Meravil protection in Ignivex and is neither Meravil nor free of the name. Conquered-house lines are not Dravon; they enter the ladder at Grade 4. Dravon is permanently barred from Vexorath and from Contair support, and the House's Council seat legalises nothing outside its own jurisdiction.

House Dravon: Ways and Sayings.text:
Dravon idiom is exact and administrative, and the family uses it on each other. "Strength should impose order" is the doctrine, said as though it were obvious. "Correct" is the only praise, and "regulation-exact" the only compliment on appearance. "Processed like anyone else" is Orvane Dravon's standard and the regime's boast, and inside the family it means nobody is exempt from audit. "The formation is the weapon" and "no duelists" are Redline teaching, said with contempt for Genesis and Volen heroics. "Mapped before fought" is Kaldor Dravon's method, applied to fronts and to relatives. "Sharpened" describes an heir under pressure, and the pressure is the point. "The gallery says" refers to Kaldor's War Gallery captions, and Vaelen Dravon uses it to mean the official story a competent person does not believe. "Defensive necessity" is the public account of both conflicts, said with a straight face in Relstaris and never at home. "Twice beaten, never dismantled" is what the House says of itself when it is being honest. "Ugly-durable" is the affectionate word for issued equipment. "Raised for the errand" describes temporary access, and "closed on the way home" what happens to someone who displeased the wrong office. "Reduced one gate at a time" is not a Dravon saying; it is what the rows say about them, and the family knows it.

House Dravon: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: records that should exist in the Red Ledger do not, and Kaldor Dravon treats it as a front to be mapped before it is fought, without knowing whom the mapping will implicate. The succession contest between Sorin Dravon and Vaelen Dravon is itself the test, with no passing grade, and Serak Dravon and Irala Dravon are being measured the same way; Kaldor keeps Soren Dravon visible as bait. Maelra Dravon keeps a second set of notes, a crime she wrote the definition of, and her sources contradict the captions in Kaldor's War Gallery. Orvane Dravon audits the machine and has never asked what he does when it points at a Dravon; the Inner Compliance Gate's processing record no longer matches what the Civic Watch Plazas report, and the discrepancy is to be carried back to him in the Red War Room. Cassor Dravon's lawful-participation project in Relstaris ends the day Dravon hands are found in a civic failure, and Kaldor is building exactly such a failure in Korrvane to provoke Ark Genesis. Kaless Nivarek watches Maelra and Orvane while records vanish from Red Ledger Prime, and whether Myrra Nivarek is the Archive's friend stays unresolved. Third-conflict planning is an intention, not an inevitable war. Let it surface through a caption that does not match a source and an audit that pauses, never as a lecture.

House Contair: Everyday Operations.text:
House Contair runs Vexorath as a set of responsibilities. Rezulith Contair holds final technical authority from Rezulith's Workshop over the Lumina Core, gate integrity, the Outer Shell and citywide defence, and decides nothing about neighbourhoods; Maelis Contair keeps civic systems usable from the Civic Systems Quarter; Drexan Contair rejects any design that cannot survive mass production and local repair at the Fabrication Yards; Tavris Contair sets drone doctrine in the Armada Holds; Solanis Contair runs Lumina Reach; Seris Contair invents independently from the Residential District and built Lumina Minor. The House also maintains every Lunar Gate on Nexara, through the Contair Maintenance Alcove in Korrvane, the Contair Inspection Post at Helvyra's hub under the Gate Compact, while Talris Contair keeps the Relstaris Core and Varis Contair sits in the Republic Council because political ignorance keeps breaking systems. Contracts pay Vexorath rates, about 85 Credits for an ordinary completed shift and 195 for a skilled one, and technology is released by risk, reproducibility, political consequence and maintenance burden; Dravon receives none. A Contair commission is an offer with terms, an offer is not acceptance, and a restriction imposed in an emergency is explained afterward.

House Contair: Signs and Membership.text:
Contair is white and charcoal seamed with cobalt, worn as technical layers with tool panels and diagnostic surfaces rather than ornament; Lumina Major is pearl-white and cobalt living alloy in the same language, and Lumina Minor is pearl-white with rose and magenta asymmetry in Seris Contair's. Both are persons, and Minor's name implies no lesser status. Custodianship is a responsibility, not a rank: a custodian acts within a field and answers afterward. A Contair surname bypasses nothing. Access to Lumina Reach follows legitimate purpose and operational responsibility, curiosity creates none, and being Contair gets nobody through the Private Lunar Gate Wing. The House officially rejects House-dominance politics and keeps its Council seat and its leverage anyway, because every gate on Nexara answers to its standard. Membership is birth or marriage and is a civic fact; Paul Thovex, Rezulith's partner, is House Thovex, and Sela Thovex stewards the Contair Compound in Relstaris without being Contair. A Contair mark on equipment says nothing until the Verification and Authenticity Station agrees, since counterfeits circulate planetwide. Drones are read by class, Ward, Mote, Aegis and Echo, and none of them is a member of anything. The tell of a real Contair is that they report their own fault first.

House Contair: Ways and Sayings.text:
Contair idiom is engineering turned on people. "A good system should make imposed order unnecessary" is the House's answer to Dravon and to anyone who wants to be obeyed. "Nothing fails the same way twice" is the promise made over every repair. "Failure is evidence, not shame" is Drexan Contair's standard, and "can it be maintained locally?" his question, which kills more prototypes than any enemy. "Records systems, not private lives" is the civic ideal, and "indirect leakage" is Maelis Contair's phrase for how it breaks. "Report the fault" means own it before someone else finds it. "Sufficient understanding" is said drily of Rezulith Contair's habit of assuming the answer is obvious once the problem is understood. "Not for release" ends a negotiation. "Possible further use" is the label on Paul Thovex's storage pod and the family's word for hoarding. "The door won" describes a visitor beaten by authentication. "Explain it after" reminds emergency authority that restrictions are reviewed once the emergency ends. "Build the alternative" is what Seris Contair does instead of arguing, and the family uses it as advice. "Every failure becomes part of the next design" is the city's consolation and its threat. Contairs greet by asking what broke, and take leave by saying what they will check.

House Contair: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: overprotection is built into the city's systems, and the line between safety and control is being tested by the House's own people. Lumina Major has refused Rezulith Contair records that Rezulith considered operational, and Rezulith accepts a medical veto she dislikes only because a system that destroys the person it was built to save is a failed system. Talris Contair has found unauthorised routing in the Relstaris Core and must ask Rezulith for help without letting Vexorath take the capitol's heart; which city the Core answers to is a question a player may be made to decide. Solanis Contair holds deep-space traffic patterns that fit no known route and announces nothing, and that stays unresolved. Maelis Contair treats indirect privacy leakage as unfinished work and has just learned that residents in the Modular Family Rows work around a system rather than report it; Paul Thovex's challenge in the Privacy Challenge Chamber is over what monitoring recorded of his own household. An Outer Shell layer has woken for a threat category nobody remembers creating. Sela Thovex's list of systems that pass review and fail residents implicates careers. Let it surface through a workaround nobody reported and a layer that woke, never as a lecture.

House Corsair: Everyday Operations.text:
House Corsair runs Helvyra by being difficult to replace. Xyren Corsair leads from Xyren's Office at the Corsair Estate, carrying the Magic Branch he trained for and the Commerce Branch he inherited from his father; Rux Corsair runs the Swordsmanship Branch from his own school across the Bladebanks. Commerce is the day's noise: Tavren Corsair works the Route Board Gallery at the Grand Waypoint, Velra Corsair collects the Dinner Tables' gossip on Merchant Row, Tavik Corsair directs the Grand Relstaris Waypoint, and Veyra Corsair keeps Dustfall supplied from Grit and Supply. Swordsmanship is morning forms, graded sparring and Vaelor Corsair drilling the advanced floor, with Korriven Corsair sent when a shipment needs someone who can read a route and survive it. Magic is Maelrix Corsair working as a guest at the Open Circle and Myris Corsair lecturing in Relstaris. Every Waypoint on Nexara, except in Quilrath, does intake, authentication, storage, courier dispatch, permit checks, claims and settlement supply under a mandatory mocking sign of Xyren's face. Couriers and dock crews earn Helvyra rates, about 70 Credits for an ordinary completed shift and 155 for a skilled one, and Courier Dispatch posts runs as offers with terms; an offer is not acceptance, and a run refused is a run refused. Stealing from a Waypoint is the one thing the House does not forgive.

House Corsair: Signs and Membership.text:
The surest Corsair sign is Xyren Corsair's face, hung by permit at every Waypoint on Nexara in a mandatory unflattering portrait that began as Contair leverage and became infrastructure; a Corsair is recognised by the joke before the name. The family dresses in burgundy and copper-toned working cloth, cargo attire with route tags for Commerce, a practical blade for Swordsmanship, layered scholar's robes for Magic, and the three branches are the real map of membership: Xyren, Tavren, Velra, Tavik and Veyra count, Rux, Vaelor, Seryn and Korriven fight, Maelrix and Myris catalogue. Membership is family, by birth or marriage, and Alcandrus Genesis, born to a Corsair mother, is Genesis. Corsair ties confer no ownership: the Open Circle is independent under Quenna Sil and Corsair members there are guests; the Common Scale is never staffed by Corsairs; Blade Courts Graded is a recognition of Rux's school, not a House rank, and a Wayline grading can be passed by anyone the school accepts. A Waypoint courier credential is a working document, and abusing it is a taboo, not a family matter. The Corsair Estate's Branch Family Guest Houses tell you which branches are thin and who has not been invited back. A Corsair surname grants no route, no seal and no standing at the Scale; what it grants is that everyone has already laughed at your face.

House Corsair: Ways and Sayings.text:
Corsair idiom is route talk. "Everything arrives. Nothing stays still" is the family's description of itself. "Read the route" means think before you commit, and in the sword school it means read the opponent's movement before the blade. "Turn the conditions" is Rux Corsair's teaching, turning circumstances into advantage, and Commerce uses it for a bad market. "Which branch?" is the first question about any Corsair and any Corsair problem. "Signed and moving" means a deal is done. "Don't touch the road" is the taboo in four words, and "Corsair forgives a bad deal, not a thief" is the long form. "Xyren's face on it" means official Corsair, and "not my sign" is Xyren's own denial of responsibility, now used by the whole family. "Useful first" is the House's view of magic and of relatives. "A route of your own" describes a child leaving the family business, said with pride and worry. "The Compact holds" is the answer to any question about the gate hub, and Torvex's name is said with the Second Dravon Conflict attached. "It's on the board" means public and therefore true enough. "Three branches, one answer" is what Xyren demands when Commerce, Swordsmanship and Magic each explain the same missing case differently. Corsairs greet with "what's moving?" and leave with "clear board."

House Corsair: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: Xyren Corsair carries Commerce he never trained for, and the missing-cargo dispute the city calls theft is, in Sereth Varriko's assembling record, insurance fraud from inside the trade network itself. Commerce counts numbers that will not reconcile, Tavren Corsair is trading against a reroute nobody ordered on the Route Board Gallery, and the consignment two cases short at the Skyhook Docks has three branch explanations. Swordsmanship argues whether the sign tradition is marketing or corrosion, and Rux Corsair would be alarmed by word of someone blending Veltrax pressure into Corsair movement, because it means the style is leaking or someone inside is freelancing; Daxor Veltrax has already read it from blade wear, and Meya Orlin has logged the wounds. Korriven Corsair keeps a record of which ambushes on the road felt staged. Magic keeps catalogues the other branches cannot read, and Maelrix Corsair keeps an exact account of everyone who mocked the craft until they needed it. The Legacy Chamber kept for Torvex Corsair at the Estate holds the Helvyra Gate Compact's obligations, and what becomes of the room is an inheritance question the family has not opened. Who is defrauding whom is not decided here. Let it surface through a branch explanation that fails and a road that felt wrong, never as a lecture.

House Volen: Everyday Operations.text:
House Volen runs Ignivex from the Emberward and holds it from everywhere else. Cynar Volen leads from the Civic Halls and speaks from the Announcement Step; Varessa Volen commands the defensive response from the Caldris Wallworks when raids, sabotage or border strikes land; Tharen Volen keeps the fortress powered from Tharen's Overseer Station in the Geothermal Core Facilities without Contair systems or imported energy; Maeryn Volen teaches breath, stance and restraint at the Crucible Yard; Selyra Volen lets grievances shout themselves out at the Smoke Court; Oryn Volen makes defiance look exciting; Iskara Volen keeps the memory in the Hearth Rows. The House leads a triangle: Caldris holds the walls and fully backs Volen, Meravil keeps the casualty records and argues for accommodation, and both reach the Emberward with their counts. In Relstaris, Tyra Volen holds the Council seat and the Volen Compound's Emergency Heat Response Bay answers fire and geothermal incidents the capitol depends on. Alerts interrupt every shift, and work is paid at Ignivex rates, about 65 Credits for an ordinary completed shift and 155 for a skilled one, when the task is finished; a watchpoint held for Varessa is an offer with terms, an offer is not acceptance, and refusing a Volen is allowed, loudly. The House holds major territory without becoming expansionist.
