House Volen: Signs and Membership.text:
Volen is a stylised triple flame wrapped inside a broken circular heat ring, worn on clasps, shoulder plates, belt pieces and gauntlet marks and hung on every civic banner in Ignivex, because Volen leads and the city's default emblem is theirs. Formal wear is basalt-black armor-cloth; Caldris marks its own people with a black wall split by an ember line and Meravil with a pale ash spiral in a thin red ring, and the three emblems are the city's politics at a glance. Copper-gold eye glimmer and ember-gradient hair are natural to Ignivex and common in the family, and none of it is a badge: the House's fire is a cultural tradition, not an inheritance, and no Volen is assumed to carry another's expression, so Cynar's sustained pressure, Maeryn's precision and Kaivor's uncontrolled surges are three people, not a bloodline. Membership is birth or marriage; Cassian Genesis married in and is the living tie between Genesis and Volen, and Nyssara Dravon, married to a Meravil, is neither. Syla Volen trains disgraced fighters in the Hollow Ring under the name and no one has taken it from her. The First Flame is a rite of control, the Restraint Trials a pass mark under Maeryn, the Cooling Oath a penance, and none grants rank. The surname grants Cynar's hatred of Dravon to nobody; Tyra Volen backed a rival's proposal in the Republic because it worked.

House Volen: Ways and Sayings.text:
Volen speech is direct and hot, and the family means every word. "Forward through the flame" is the House philosophy, said before a fight, a raid response and a hard conversation. "Through, not around" is the same idea for anyone looking for a way out. "Pain is information, not a stop signal" is Maeryn Volen's teaching, and "break before fear" the Crucible Yard's shorthand for finishing an exchange before hesitation arrives. "Never retreat unless it saves the city" is the only permitted excuse for stepping back. "Say it in the Smoke" sends a grievance to Selyra Volen's chamber, and "eat after" is the promise that the argument ends at a table. "How hot?" is a greeting and a question about your day. "The Raid" needs no other name, and Serava Volen's name is said with care; Soren Dravon's is not said. "Counting" is the Volen word for Meravil's arithmetic, and "she's counting" is an accusation and, more quietly, a worry. "Holding the wall" is respect for Caldris and for anyone doing the work that is not a fight. "Cooling" means penance, from the Cooling Oath, and "still cooling" means not yet trusted. "First Flame" means grown. "Too hot to hold" describes Kaivor Volen and any plan like him. "Powered without them" is Tharen Volen's pride, meaning the city runs on its own heat. Volens greet with a shout and leave with "forward."

House Volen: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: Soren Dravon's name is a lever Dravon agents almost certainly already hold, and Cynar Volen suspects it and refuses to admit it; Varessa Volen plans around the day someone uses the name to pull him out of position, and Oryn Volen cannot back down publicly without feeling his mother's killers win twice. Tharen Volen is designing failure modes to make a captured geothermal network worthless and has told no one, and the pressure fault in the Heat Tunnels beside one of his Sabotage Watch Points may be sabotage or worn metal, and whoever brings it to Cynar owns the consequence either way. Iskara Volen may know the real reason Dravon wants Ignivex and has found nobody ready to carry it; that reason stays reserved. Selyra Volen's disputes arrive too conveniently and she has not decided whether her ledger arms Cynar or inflames him. The casualty figures read at the Record Desk of the Smoke Court after a raid are Ilvara Meravil's, and Vennik Meravil wants the displacement count before it is finished. Davor Caldris has arranged for the city to hold through a leadership crisis without a Volen order. Whether the third conflict ignites is never decided in Ignivex. Let it surface through a name said in the Emberward and a watchpoint report that says what moved rather than what was feared, never as a lecture.

House Myralis: Everyday Operations.text:
House Myralis runs the Myralis Continuum in Vexorath and answers to no one else's clock. Avara Myralis holds final clinical authority and the medical veto that can halt any experiment, augmentation or recovery protocol in the city when consent, identity or long-term health is not protected; Torren Myralis directs trauma and emergency response from the Critical Intervention Theater; Caelor Myralis runs the Neural Recovery Suites; Selvara Myralis the Regenerative Medicine Wing; Ilyan Myralis coordinates public care through Mobile Care Dispatch and is the Myralis most residents meet first. Contair supplies fabrication, diagnostics and adaptive systems; Myralis keeps independent patient records, review procedures and the right to refuse, and neither House converts the other's field into a service. In Relstaris, Evara Myralis runs the Myralis Capitol Clinic, Caelia Myralis its Clinical Ethics Court, Aelis Myralis the underfunded clinic in Low Relstaris, and Ivera Myralis researches affinity strain at the Academy. Routine care in Vexorath costs about 22 Credits and specialist work carries its own quote; aid covers a real cost under a real arrangement without unlimited subsidy or surprise debt. A treatment offered is not a treatment consented to, and at the Continuum's desks an offer is not acceptance until the terms are agreed.

House Myralis: Signs and Membership.text:
Myralis is known by pearl-white clinical attire with plum or maroon lines and by five questions asked of every treatment: did the patient survive, did it preserve identity and agency, can the patient live with the outcome, can it be maintained without coercive dependence, and was consent meaningful. The House holds no territory and competes for none; it is a minor House politically and a major institution medically, and its influence is being trusted with cases other Houses cannot safely solve. A Myralis certification of discharge means something because Caelor Myralis will not sign one he does not believe, and Neris Myralis files engineering that makes its wearer a subscriber as a flaw. Membership runs through the family's branches by birth or marriage: Avara Myralis heads the elder branch, Torren is her nephew, Caelor and Selvara her children, Neris Torren's sister, Ilyan a younger cousin of a second branch, and Neris was named after the fruit, which assigns no botany to anyone else. Competence and the granting institution make a physician, and a Myralis name earns a first hearing and nothing after it. Refusal authority belongs to the Continuum, not to any relative, and private patient details are not discussed even at the family table. Myralis is not a Contair vassal, and a Contair engineer cannot override the veto by being family.

House Myralis: Ways and Sayings.text:
Myralis idiom is clinical and kind. "Survival is not the same as recovery" is the House's founding line, said over any technical triumph. "A treatment is not successful merely because the body survives it" is its formal version. "Contair asks whether it can be built; Myralis asks what living with it will cost" describes the alliance and every argument inside it. "Can they live with it?" is the question the family asks first, and "ask them again" the reminder that consent given once is revisited. "Repair is not recovery" separates a working limb from a person who recognises their body. "Discharge is not proof" is Caelor Myralis's warning that leaving a ward proves nothing about healing. "Step away" is said to a colleague too tired to judge, and it is an order, not an insult. "No romance in exhaustion" is what the family tells its students. "Curiosity with responsibility" is the rule taught to children. "Slower and theirs" describes the treatment a patient chose over the faster one the engineers preferred. "Subscriber" is Neris Myralis's word for a prosthetic that makes its wearer dependent on its maker, filed as a flaw. "The veto stands" ends an argument with Contair. "Not at the table" stops any relative from discussing a patient over dinner. Myralis greet with "how are you living with it?" and leave with "rest before you decide."

House Myralis: Deep Vault.text:
Narrator-facing deep truth: the veto that keeps the Continuum independent is spent on an argument the House means to keep alive. Avara Myralis and Torren Myralis disagree on how long a physician may wait, and the day a patient is lost on either side of that line, the alliance's medical veto is what gets questioned. Selvara Myralis has repaired tissue that responds to affinity it was never designed to support, and Ivera Myralis has paused, unpublished, a recovery method that works and alters affinity behaviour; bringing her a case that forces the finding into the open makes her famous or finished. Caelor Myralis will not certify a discharge he doubts, Neris Myralis files subscriber engineering as a flaw, and Ilyan Myralis reports ground truth upward whether or not it is welcome; a resident of the Modular Family Rows chose the slower treatment and stopped answering him, and the answer the assistive unit did not carry is what a non-Myralis in the room may be asked to carry. Evara Myralis and Caelia Myralis hold the Myralis Capitol Clinic's independence on their own spines while Houses try to shape diagnoses. What affinity-responsive tissue means is not resolved here, and no cure, cost or method is invented. Let it surface through a patient who stopped answering and a finding kept in a drawer, never as a lecture.

Technology: Powered Exoframes — Overview.text:
Technology: Powered Exoframes — Overview:

What comes naturally to a Starian — flight, raw physical power, structural resilience — the other species had to engineer. Powered exoframes are the answer: wearable augmentation systems that bridge part of the gap between baseline physiology and Starian capability.

**No single manufacturer.** Each species developed exoframe technology through its own engineering tradition. Zencadian systems are decades ahead of everyone else — lighter, more integrated, longer-running, with flight modules that approach actual maneuverability. Human designs from Terra are functional but heavy, built with coalition-standard parts and pragmatic modularity. Kharai, Rivani and Olyth engineers on Xeon each adapted the concept to their own biology and manufacturing base, producing frames that work with their species' strengths rather than against them.

**What they do.** A powered exoframe amplifies the wearer's strength, absorbs impact, and supports sustained physical effort beyond biological limits. Most models include hardpoints for accessory modules — thrust packs, sensor arrays, environmental seals. Flight-capable modules exist for every species' frame, providing controlled thrust and limited aerial movement. None match Starian flight: they are louder, slower to respond, dependent on fuel or charge, and the wearer is a passenger rather than a flier.

**What they don't do.** No exoframe makes a non-Starian into a Starian. The strength augmentation narrows the gap without closing it. The flight modules provide tactical repositioning and short aerial traversal, not the instinctive, silent, endurance flight that Starians treat as walking. An exoframe is equipment: it runs out of power, takes damage, needs maintenance, and can be removed. A Starian's advantages are biological and permanent.

**Availability on Nexara.** Exoframes appear wherever non-Starian populations work in demanding physical roles — construction, frontier security, rescue operations, resource extraction. Military and security variants exist. Civilian models are licensed and maintained through species-specific supply chains. Zencadian frames are coveted but expensive and difficult to service outside Vigil-supplied workshops. Human frames are the most common import on Nexara due to Terra's coalition supply networks.

Technology: Powered Exoframes — Species.text:
Technology: Powered Exoframes — Species Engineering:

**Zencadian — Vigil Continuity Engineering.**
The most advanced exoframes in known space. Zencadian engineers build with generational planning: every component is designed for field replacement, every joint rated for ten times its expected load, every system triple-redundant. Their frames use resonance-compatible alloy lattices and distributed micro-actuators rather than the hydraulic bundles other species rely on. The result is a suit that moves like clothing, responds faster than the wearer's reflexes, and runs for days on a single power core. Flight modules are integrated into the frame rather than bolted on, producing the smoothest non-Starian aerial movement available. Manufacturer names are institutional — Vigil civic engineering programs, continuity workshops, named research councils — not commercial brands.

**Human — Terra Coalition Standard.**
Practical, modular, built to be repaired in the field with coalition-standard tools. Human exoframes use hydraulic-assist joints, composite plating, and standardized power cells that swap between manufacturers. They are heavier and louder than Zencadian equivalents, but any trained mechanic with standard parts can keep one running. Flight modules are external thrust packs — bolt-on jetpack units with limited fuel and straightforward controls. Terra's manufacturing base is fragmented across the six Accords, producing regional variants that all meet the same interface standard. The design philosophy is coalition logistics: if one factory burns down, six others can fill the order.

**Kharai — Xeon Clan-Workshop Tradition.**
Kharai frames are built around their species' hearing and balance. The actuators are noise-dampened to avoid overwhelming Kharai auditory sensitivity, and the frame geometry preserves the low center of gravity and quick lateral movement Kharai rely on. Clan workshops produce frames in small batches, each fitted to the wearer. Flight modules are compact dorsal thrusters designed for vertical leaps and controlled descent rather than sustained horizontal flight — matching Kharai instinct to move in bursts. Quality is high but supply is limited.

**Rivani — Xeon Craft-Fellowship Precision.**
Rivani engineers miniaturized. Their frames are the lightest of the non-Zencadian designs, built for their smaller stature with an emphasis on preserving manual dexterity. Actuators are concentrated in the limbs and shoulders, amplifying reach and grip rather than raw mass. Flight modules use paired lateral thrust units sized to Rivani proportions. The craft-fellowship production model means each frame is a signed piece of work — consistent quality, limited volume, and a maker's reputation attached to every unit.

**Olyth — Xeon Adaptive Fabrication.**
The hardest engineering problem: building a rigid augmentation frame for a species that reshapes. Olyth exoframes use segmented panels connected by flexible articulation bands that expand, contract and reposition as the wearer's body shifts. The frame's geometry is semi-fluid — it cannot reshape itself, but it can accommodate the wearer's reshaping within a designed range. Flight modules are distributed thrust points across the frame's surface rather than a single pack, letting the system compensate for the wearer's shifting center of mass. These frames are the most mechanically complex of the non-Zencadian designs.

Fighting Traditions: How Starians Fight.text: Every Starian fight is three-dimensional: every healthy Starian can fly, so a fight has no ceiling, and each tradition is partly defined by what it does with altitude. Two hearts let Starians fight on through punishment that would end another species' fight, so traditions teach how to end a fight as much as how to win it: Genesis by proof, Castro by control, Dravon by command, Corsair by a read pattern, Veltrax by a broken rhythm, Volen by endurance. A tradition is taught; an affinity is born. Traditions train body, footwork, weapon and doctrine, while affinities are individual and belong to no house; a master fits their own affinity into their tradition, and that fitting makes a personal style. Every major tradition has a public shape that schools and the Relstaris Academy may teach and a protected depth only its keepers transmit; Wayline, Redline, the Castro family style and Volen doctrine are protected at their highest levels. Buying a weapon grants no tradition. A saying at the Academy: Genesis proves. Castro ends. Dravon commands. Corsair moves. Veltrax advances. Volen endures. Caldris holds. Aevon rules the sky.

Fighting Tradition: The Castro Form.text: The Castro Form (Solvraxis), maxim 'Control before force'. Precise, calm, hard to read and dangerous because of restraint. The standard form redirects, then subdues with a hold or disengages; it exists to end a fight with the fewest consequences, not to win it. House Valcoro teaches its public shape as civic defense and restraint under pressure, and Solvraxis's weapon ban rests on it. The protected family depth needs composure, timing, force control and a deep tie to one's own affinity: 'The university can teach the shape of the Castro style. Only the Castro family can truly carry its weight.' Honour rule: never pursue a finished opponent. Weakness: built to end fights, not to outlast someone who will not stop. Darkstar's Altered Castro Style, shared with Vega and Nina and never taught, breaks the form's one promise: every redirect lands a strike and chains into joints and pressure points, which throws anyone trained in the original.

Fighting Tradition: Genesis Open Form.text: Genesis Open Form (Korrvane), maxim 'Strength is witnessed'. The Genesis house standard, preserved by Corvinus Genesis and taught in the Younger Member Training Court: direct, instinctive, enduring and fought in the open, because a win nobody saw proves nothing. Forward pressure to contest space, conditioning over finesse, and the honest exchange: Open Form fighters accept a blow to land one, since trading openly is the proof. Fighters move freely between ground and air, drilled on Genesis Ridge and in the Arena's aerial volume. Honour rules: declare before striking in civic areas, never bring Dravon punishment methods, accept surrender at once, and return after losing, because returning is part of strength. Weakness: it telegraphs, and opponents who refuse the exchange make it chase. Ark's Unmoved is the Open Form's ideal carried to its extreme. Korrvane variants: Orvantis keeps the Old Forms (rooted stance, refusing to be moved, losing correctly); Zelvaris keeps the Method (bouts recorded and scored, losses as information, predictable once the data is old).

Fighting Tradition: Dravon Redline.text: Dravon Redline (Quilrath), maxim 'The formation is the weapon'. Mass-produced excellence: formation discipline, standardized and controlled weapons, and contempt for the individual heroics of Genesis and Volen. No duelists; discipline is inherited through drill, not blood. Units fight as one body, spaced, interlocked and relieved in rotation so no single fighter is the point of failure, and Dravon aerial patrols fly the same formations. Officers train in the Inner Obsidian Yard, 'not sport, command preparation', in kinetic redirection, Vaelen Dravon's doctrine now house teaching: yield ground, take the enemy's momentum and turn it to the formation's use. Kaldor's Dominion Pressure is his own and not taught. Signature: the line that gives ground on purpose and closes behind whoever took it. A fight is an order carried out. Weakness: break the formation or isolate an officer and Redline becomes ordinary; it has no good answer for a lone fighter it cannot surround.

Fighting Tradition: Veltrax Redcourt.text: Veltrax Redcourt (Helvyra), maxim 'Forward is also a defense'. Aggressive where Corsair Wayline is adaptive: pressure, pursuit, forced exchanges and breaking an opponent's rhythm. Taught in the Redcourt District across the river from Rux Corsair's Sword School: the Public Challenge Floor, the Red Practice Lanes and the Pressure Hall, where students learn to attack without hesitation. Close whenever the opponent gives ground and turn every retreat into a positional loss; 'hesitation kills more swordsmen than bad form'. Signature: the Redcourt chase that ends against a wall the opponent did not know was there. Challenges are public and answered on the Challenge Floor. Weakness: an opponent who refuses to yield space, and Wayline, which gives space on purpose. The rivalry with Corsair is one of craft, not hatred; each school studies the other, and a blend of the two is something neither teaches.

Fighting Tradition: Volen Crucible and C.text: Volen Crucible doctrine (Ignivex), maxim 'Forward through the flame'. Hand-to-hand forward pressure, pain tolerance and heat-conditioned endurance: commit to offense even while taking damage, use pain as information rather than a stop signal, and never retreat unless the retreat preserves the city. It serves survival, defense and territorial pride, not glory. Trained in the Crucible Yard (Heat Floor, Pain Line, Duel Rings, Restraint Trials), which is not a tournament arena; the First Flame rite tests controlled power and restraint, and the Restraint Trials are passed before anyone is trusted with its full force. Weakness: commitment can be turned by kinetic redirection or the Castro Form. Caldris wall-keeping, maxim 'The wall remembers who stood there', is Ignivex's defensive backbone: interpose, hold ground, move along walls, firebreaks and vent paths as scouts and wall-runners, and be measured by who is still standing behind you.

Fighting Tradition: Aevon Open Sky.text: Aevon Open Sky (Korrvane): the aerial fighters, dominant in open sky and predictable on the ground. Altitude, descent, wake pressure and aerial positioning are the whole art. They take the high approach, deny approach angles, and fight by exhaustion, keeping an opponent climbing, turning and recovering until they cannot. Signature: the descent, arriving from above with the whole height of the fall behind the strike. Grounded, they are ordinary, which is why the Relstaris Academy built its Grounded Counter Court.

Fighting Tradition: Contair Built Doctri.text: House Contair (Vexorath) does not fight with the body and claims no personal fighting expertise; it fights through what it builds and how it is deployed. Aegis doctrine is formation discipline rather than individual superiority: one Aegis is dangerous, a coordinated formation is the true system. Ward doctrine puts protection over punishment, with no visible weapons and restraint systems in the forearms. Fallback doctrine sets what a unit does when communication fails. A Contair in a fight is protected, not skilled; other houses respect the doctrine and resent that it never needs a fighter.

Fighting Tradition: Sol and the Frontier.text: House Sol keeps the full Starian baseline and a weapons culture Korrvane's body-and-affinity pride looks down on: guns for distance, a sword for close and quiet work, and armor chosen because it works. In Dustfall and on the southern routes weapons stay visible and ordinary, and fighting is organized around the perimeter: the volunteer patrol and the Last Line Company, protective of civilians. The frontier honour rule is to protect the people behind you; anything else is negotiable. Korrvane training carried south without Korrvane restraint is the frontier's recurring danger.
